Marketing Strategy & Management in the Global Company 
2026 BIZ 3007 Syllabus 
 
 
 
Professor: 심수옥 
Office: 33313 
 
 
Course Objectives 
글로벌 기업의 마케팅 전략 개발 및 집행 과정에서 논의되는 주요 이슈들과 의사 결정 
과정에 대한 이해를 높이고 실무 역량을 함양하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 
 
수업은 글로벌 기업의 마케팅 전략 개발에 사용되는 핵심적인 마케팅의 개념 및 틀에 
대한 학습, 급변하는 글로벌 환경 속에서 중요성이 높아지는 마케팅 이슈에 관한 
토의를 주요 내용으로 하여 진행됩니다. 학생들은 수업 중 학습한 개념과 사례를 
적용하여 실제 기업의 마케팅 전략과 실행  사례를 분석 , 평가하고 개선점을 
도출하는 마케팅 프로젝트를 수행합니다. 
 
 
This course offers an introduction to marketing practices in a real world. The main objectives 
of the course are to: (1) introduce core marketing concepts and tools that are crucial to develop 
marketing strategies and execution in the global company, (2) develop an understanding of 
changing business environment surrounding global companies, and (3) provide a forum to 
discuss current marketing issues faced by a global organization. 
 
Class Format 
The class consists of a series of lectures, case presentation, and discussion. We will use many 
different materials in the course – articles from popular press, academic journals, and books. 
Those will be presented in lectures and discussions. 
 
 
이 수업은 PBL (Project-based Learning) 수업 방식으로 진행됩니다.  전반부에는  
핵심적인 마케팅 개념을 학습하고 프로젝트 수행을 위한 사례 연구 및 토론을 
진행하고 수업 후반부 4주간 학습한 내용을 적용하여 기업의 마케팅 과제를 수행하며 
과제는 기말 시험을 대체합니다. 2026년도 2학기에 수행할 과제는 현 대 카 드 에 서 
최 근 출 시 한 알 파 벳 카 드 마 케 팅 프 로 젝 트 로 1 주차 수업에서 구 체 적 
과 제 를 소 개 합 니 다.  
수업은 월요일12:00-13:15은 온라인으로 동영상 시청 및 과제 제출 방식으로  진행되고 
수요일 13:30-14:45은 오프라인으로 발표 및 토론을 진행합니다
. 
 
Course Materials 
 Assigned reading articles will be uploaded at iCampus. 
 
 
Course Requirement 
Evaluation 
 Class Attendance (10%) 
 Group Assignment & In-Class participation (20%) 
 Mid-term Test (30%) 
 Team Marketing Project (40%) 
 
 
Class Participation 
 
Students are expected to read the assigned readings, take part in pertinent discussion, listen to 
others with respect during the team discussion. I will keep notes regarding each student’s 
contributions in class and aggregate all the marks at the end of the course to decide on an overall 
participation grade. In addition, peer evaluation of the assigned team will be conducted and 
reflected into individual grading. 
 
Individual Assignment 
Each student will be assigned on a case analysis or research of a subject during the course. A 
list of assignments will be posted on i-campus when the class begins. 
 
Marketing Project 
You will work with your group on a real -life marketing proble m facing one of the global 
company marketing team. All of the details of the  marketing project will be made with a visit 
from a key member of the company marketing team during a special session.  The formal 
requirements will be a written report recommending  a course of action addressing the 
challenges set out in the assignment brief and a short 15 minute oral presentation at the end of 
the semester, which will be attended by the company’s senior marketing executives.

exactFullPublicAttachmentEducation.educationFullText:
BIZ 3012 비즈니스 캡스톤 디자인 
Fall 2026 Syllabus 
 
 
Professor: Sue Shim 심수옥 
Office: 33313 
 
 
Course Description and Objectives 
 
새로운 상품 및 서비스/경험을 개발하는데 적용하는 주요 원칙과 최신 접근법을 
배우고 시장조사와 분석, 소비자 리서치 과제를 수행하고 소비자  
니즈/ 인사이트 기반  Ideation, Storytelling 방법과 사례 연구를 진행합니다.  
기업의 실제 과제를 진행하며 기업의 업무 방식을 간접적으로 배우고 경험하는 
기회가 될 것입니다. 학생들은 4-5 명이 한 조가 되어 프로젝트를 수행하고 학기말에 
임원 진에게 결과물을 발표하고 평가를 받습니다. 
 
2026년도 2학기에는 LG 전자 오디오 사업부의 신상품/솔루션  기획 과제를 수행할 
예정입니다
.  이번 학기에는 기존 산학 과제의 제품 중심 상품 기획에서 솔루션 
제안으로 주제를 확대하여 진행합니다.  과제는 음악 청취/연주 또는 음악 기반 
엔터테인먼트 관련 소비자의 니즈를 해결할 수 있는 오디오 솔루션 제안입니다.  
다양한 장르의 음악 관련 분야에 관심이 있는 전공/비전공 학생 모두 환영합니다.   
 
주차별 수업은 다음과 같이 진행됩니다. 
 
1-4주 Design Thinking Process 학습. Consumer Research Methodology - AI 활용 
포함하여 학습합니다. 
4-8 주 LG 전자 소비자 데이터 분석
 . Insight 발굴 
9-12주 Generative Questions 기반 Ideation 
13-16주 Prototyping. 및 발표
 
 
이번 학기에는 강의 또는 단체 활동 보다는 팀별 피드백 세션을 중심으로 진행할 
예정입니다.  LG전자 오디오 사업부 사업부장 및 (전) 삼성전자 Product Innovation 
담당 임원들의 특강 및 Q&A 세션을 진행합니다. 
 
 
 
 
Classs Format 
• Lectures 
• Semester long team-based projects 
• Student led discussions and workshops 
• Participatory presentation and open critique sessions 
 
Course Materials 
• Tom Kelly & David Kelly, Unleashing the Creative Potential (2021), IDEO 아이디오는 
어떻게 디자인하는가 스탠퍼드 디스쿨 창조성 수업 
 
Grading 
수업 유형 : PBL 
Grades will be weighted as follows: 
• Attendance and In-class Participation (30%) 
• Group Project (70%)

publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: 강의 내용은 사전에 동영상으로 촬영한 온라인 이론 강의를 통해서 전달한다. 학생들은 교재인 ‘현대마케팅(제 10 판, 2026) ’을 읽고, 교재의 내용을 이해하고 수업에 참여해야 한다. 또한 학생들은 해당 주차의 온라인강의를 미리 듣고 수업에 와야 하고, 온라인 강의 수강 여부는 온라인 출석으로 체크한다. 2. 오프라인 수업에서는 해당 주차의 강의 내용을 중심으로 학생들이 제출하는 사전질문을 중심으로 진행한다. 그리고 오프라인 수업에서는 해당하는 주차의 강의내용을 바탕으로 학생들이 제출하는 사전질문에 적용해서 토론을 한다. Ⅱ. 교재(필수) -3- 유필화 김용준 한상만(2026), 현대마케팅론(10 판) 박영사 III. AI 사용 지침 - AI 사용은 학습 경험 및 지식을 확장하기 위해서 활용해야 한다. 모든 과제 및 질문의 생성 과정에서 학생 스스로의 창의성을 유지해야 하며 AI 에 전적으로 의존하지 않고, AI의 결과물을 학생 본인의 학습경험과 지식을 확장하는 데 활용해야 하며, 특히, AI의 활용에 있어서는 학생 스스로의 생각과 관점, 즉 창의성이 들어가야 한다. - AI 의 결과물을 사전과제에 그대로 활용하는 경우 사전과제로 인정되지 않는다. AI 결과물을 그대로 제출하는 것이 발견되면 감점(수업 참여도에서 감점) 대상이 된다. IV. 수업참여도 매시간 강의의 내용과 학생들이 올리는 사전 질문들 중에서 선정하여 토의를 한다. 수업시간의 한계로 모든 사전 질문에 대한 토의를 하지는 않는다. (1) 사전 질문: 학생들은 수업시간 전에 해당 주차의 온라인 강의를 듣고 수업에 임해야 한다. 1. 온라인 강의를 듣고 이해되지 않은 내용에 대한 질문, 혹은 수업 내용을 기반으로 연계되는 질문 (0.5 점 ~ 1점) 2. 그 주차의 수업과 관련되는 자료를 찾아서 실제 사례에 적용하여 토론 주제를 제시하는 질문 (1.0 점) (주의: AI 결과물을 자신의 생각과 관점의 적용 없이 그대로 제출하는 경우 감점 대상) 3. 수업시간에 토론 주제로 선정된 질문 (1.5점) -4- 사전 질문은 아이캠퍼스의 토론방에 제출한다. 강의 동영상은 수업 주의 전주 월요일부터 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업주의 일요일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다. (예를 들어, 3 월 17일(화) 수업을 위한 강의동영상은 전주 월요일인 3 월 9 일에 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업 주의 일요일인 3 월 15 일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다) (2) 토론 주제: 토론 주제는 학생들의 사전 질문 중에서 선정하는 것으로 하지만, 교수가 토론주제를 제안하거나 수정할 수 있다. 선정된 토론주제는 수업 당일 수업 전에 올리는 것을 원칙으로 하며, 학생들은 토론 주제를 미리 확인하고, 자신의 생각을 정리하여 수업에 임해야 한다. (학생들이 올린 사전질문과 토론주제는 아이캠퍼스의 열린 게시판에서 확인한다) 학생들은 적극적인 태도로 토의에 참여하고 의견을 제시하는 것은 수업참여도 점수에 반영된다. 각 수업에서의 참여도는 참여의 정도에 따라서 매 수업마다 0 점, 0.5 점, 1 점, 1.5 점(최대)으로 반영된다. (3) Grading: 수업참여도는 다음과 같이 정한다. A+: 100, A: 90, B+: 80, B: 70, C+: 60, C: 50, D+: 40, D: 30, F: 10 참여도 점수의 총점을 기준으로 위와 같이 A+부터 F 로 grade를 주고, 이를 30 점 만점으로 환산한다. V. 수업 출석 10 점 만점의 참여도 점수에서 온라인 결석은 각 0.5 점씩, 오프라인의 결석은 각 1 점씩 차감한다. -5- 온라인과 오프라인을 합한 결석 점수가 7 점을 넘으면 전체 성적은 F 로 한다. (특별한 사유로 수업에 참석을 못하는 경우, 교수의 재량으로 최대 1 회까지 출석 인정으로 할 수 있다. 관련 증빙서류를 첨부하여 조교에게 전달해야 한다.) VI. 중간고사, 기말고사 중간고사 성적이 F 일 경우, 전체 성적을 F 처리한다. (결시는 F 로 처리한다.) VII. 강의 내용을 중심으로 학생들이 제출하는 사전질문을 중심으로 진행한다. 그리고 오프라인 수업에서는 해당하는 주차의 강의내용을 바탕으로 학생들이 제출하는 사전질문에 적용해서 토론을 한다. Ⅱ. 교재(필수) -3- 유필화 김용준 한상만(2026), 현대마케팅론(10 판) 박영사 III. AI 사용 지침 - AI 사용은 학습 경험 및 지식을 확장하기 위해서 활용해야 한다. 모든 과제 및 질문의 생성 과정에서 학생 스스로의 창의성을 유지해야 하며 AI 에 전적으로 의존하지 않고, AI의 결과물을 학생 본인의 학습경험과 지식을 확장하는 데 활용해야 하며, 특히, AI의 활용에 있어서는 학생 스스로의 생각과 관점, 즉 창의성이 들어가야 한다. - AI 의 결과물을 사전과제에 그대로 활용하는 경우 사전과제로 인정되지 않는다. AI 결과물을 그대로 제출하는 것이 발견되면 감점(수업 참여도에서 감점) 대상이 된다. IV. 수업참여도 매시간 강의의 내용과 학생들이 올리는 사전 질문들 중에서 선정하여 토의를 한다. 수업시간의 한계로 모든 사전 질문에 대한 토의를 하지는 않는다. (1) 사전 질문: 학생들은 수업시간 전에 해당 주차의 온라인 강의를 듣고 수업에 임해야 한다. 1. 온라인 강의를 듣고 이해되지 않은 내용에 대한 질문, 혹은 수업 내용을 기반으로 연계되는 질문 (0.5 점 ~ 1점) 2. 그 주차의 수업과 관련되는 자료를 찾아서 실제 사례에 적용하여 토론 주제를 제시하는 질문 (1.0 점) (주의: AI 결과물을 자신의 생각과 관점의 적용 없이 그대로 제출하는 경우 감점 대상) 3. 수업시간에 토론 주제로 선정된 질문 (1.5점) -4- 사전 질문은 아이캠퍼스의 토론방에 제출한다. 강의 동영상은 수업 주의 전주 월요일부터 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업주의 일요일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다. (예를 들어, 3 월 17일(화) 수업을 위한 강의동영상은 전주 월요일인 3 월 9 일에 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업 주의 일요일인 3 월 15 일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다) (2) 토론 주제: 토론 주제는 학생들의 사전 질문 중에서 선정하는 것으로 하지만, 교수가 토론주제를 제안하거나 수정할 수 있다. 선정된 토론주제는 수업 당일 수업 전에 올리는 것을 원칙으로 하며, 학생들은 토론 주제를 미리 확인하고, 자신의 생각을 정리하여 수업에 임해야 한다. (학생들이 올린 사전질문과 토론주제는 아이캠퍼스의 열린 게시판에서 확인한다) 학생들은 적극적인 태도로 토의에 참여하고 의견을 제시하는 것은 수업참여도 점수에 반영된다. 각 수업에서의 참여도는 참여의 정도에 따라서 매 수업마다 0 점, 0.5 점, 1 점, 1.5 점(최대)으로 반영된다. (3) Grading: 수업참여도는 다음과 같이 정한다. A+: 100, A: 90, B+: 80, B: 70, C+: 60, C: 50, D+: 40, D: 30, F: 10 참여도 점수의 총점을 기준으로 위와 같이 A+부터 F 로 grade를 주고, 이를 30 점 만점으로 환산한다. V. 수업 출석 10 점 만점의 참여도 점수에서 온라인 결석은 각 0.5 점씩, 오프라인의 결석은 각 1 점씩 차감한다. -5- 온라인과 오프라인을 합한 결석 점수가 7 점을 넘으면 전체 성적은 F 로 한다. (특별한 사유로 수업에 참석을 못하는 경우, 교수의 재량으로 최대 1 회까지 출석 인정으로 할 수 있다. 관련 증빙서류를 첨부하여 조교에게 전달해야 한다.) VI. 중간고사, 기말고사 중간고사 성적이 F 일 경우, 전체 성적을 F 처리한다. (결시는 F 로 처리한다.) VII. AI 사용 지침 - AI 사용은 학습 경험 및 지식을 확장하기 위해서 활용해야 한다. 모든 과제 및 질문의 생성 과정에서 학생 스스로의 창의성을 유지해야 하며 AI 에 전적으로 의존하지 않고, AI의 결과물을 학생 본인의 학습경험과 지식을 확장하는 데 활용해야 하며, 특히, AI의 활용에 있어서는 학생 스스로의 생각과 관점, 즉 창의성이 들어가야 한다. - AI 의 결과물을 사전과제에 그대로 활용하는 경우 사전과제로 인정되지 않는다. AI 결과물을 그대로 제출하는 것이 발견되면 감점(수업 참여도에서 감점) 대상이 된다. IV. 수업참여도 매시간 강의의 내용과 학생들이 올리는 사전 질문들 중에서 선정하여 토의를 한다. 수업시간의 한계로 모든 사전 질문에 대한 토의를 하지는 않는다. (1) 사전 질문: 학생들은 수업시간 전에 해당 주차의 온라인 강의를 듣고 수업에 임해야 한다. 1. 온라인 강의를 듣고 이해되지 않은 내용에 대한 질문, 혹은 수업 내용을 기반으로 연계되는 질문 (0.5 점 ~ 1점) 2. 그 주차의 수업과 관련되는 자료를 찾아서 실제 사례에 적용하여 토론 주제를 제시하는 질문 (1.0 점) (주의: AI 결과물을 자신의 생각과 관점의 적용 없이 그대로 제출하는 경우 감점 대상) 3. 수업시간에 토론 주제로 선정된 질문 (1.5점) -4- 사전 질문은 아이캠퍼스의 토론방에 제출한다. 강의 동영상은 수업 주의 전주 월요일부터 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업주의 일요일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다. (예를 들어, 3 월 17일(화) 수업을 위한 강의동영상은 전주 월요일인 3 월 9 일에 게시되고, 사전질문은 수업 주의 일요일인 3 월 15 일 정오(12시)까지 올려야 한다) (2) 토론 주제: 토론 주제는 학생들의 사전 질문 중에서 선정하는 것으로 하지만, 교수가 토론주제를 제안하거나 수정할 수 있다. 선정된 토론주제는 수업 당일 수업 전에 올리는 것을 원칙으로 하며, 학생들은 토론 주제를 미리 확인하고, 자신의 생각을 정리하여 수업에 임해야 한다. (학생들이 올린 사전질문과 토론주제는 아이캠퍼스의 열린 게시판에서 확인한다) 학생들은 적극적인 태도로 토의에 참여하고 의견을 제시하는 것은 수업참여도 점수에 반영된다. 각 수업에서의 참여도는 참여의 정도에 따라서 매 수업마다 0 점, 0.5 점, 1 점, 1.5 점(최대)으로 반영된다. (3) Grading: 수업참여도는 다음과 같이 정한다. A+: 100, A: 90, B+: 80, B: 70, C+: 60, C: 50, D+: 40, D: 30, F: 10 참여도 점수의 총점을 기준으로 위와 같이 A+부터 F 로 grade를 주고, 이를 30 점 만점으로 환산한다. V. 수업 출석 10 점 만점의 참여도 점수에서 온라인 결석은 각 0.5 점씩, 오프라인의 결석은 각 1 점씩 차감한다. -5- 온라인과 오프라인을 합한 결석 점수가 7 점을 넘으면 전체 성적은 F 로 한다. (특별한 사유로 수업에 참석을 못하는 경우, 교수의 재량으로 최대 1 회까지 출석 인정으로 할 수 있다. 관련 증빙서류를 첨부하여 조교에게 전달해야 한다.) VI. 중간고사, 기말고사 중간고사 성적이 F 일 경우, 전체 성적을 F 처리한다. (결시는 F 로 처리한다.) VII. MARKETING MANAGEMENT FALL 2026 Class format: Flip Learning Time: M 09:00-10:15 am / W 10:30-11:45 am Wednesday classes will be held live offline. Professor: Jerry Jisang Han E-mail: [비공개 정보 제거] Office Hours: By appointment only: Send me a short email in advance about when you would like to meet and what you would like t
publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: 1) Identify and apply the key tools marketers use to deal with marketing issues. 2) Apply the key principles and use terminology marketers use to discuss marketing issues. 3) Connect the knowledge of marketing to real-world events. 4) Understand the role of marketing in society and in an economic system. 5) Understand the role of marketing in a firm and the relationships between marketing and the other functional areas of business (e.g., accounting, finance, MIS, management). CLASS FORMAT AND POLICIES Class sessions will include lectures, guest speaker talks, discussions of business cases and business press articles, and in class exercises. I expect you to conduct yourselves professionally. You should respect both your classmates and the instructor. This includes arriving to class on time, turning off and putting away your cell phones, refraining from conducting personal conversations, and maintaining a courteous attitude towards your classmates and the instructor. Students who are unruly, unprofessional, or is a negative influence on the class’s learning environment can and will be removed from class with or without warning. GRADING Attendance & Class Contribution 15 % Midterm Proposal Presentation 5 % Midterm Exam 25 % Team Project Report 10 % Team Project Final Presentation 15 % Peer Evaluation -5 ~ 5 % Final Exam 25 % Total 100 % Note: Any questions / appeals in regards to marks or grades must be made within 5 days of it being posted online. For fairness and to root out grade fishing behavior, all appeals should be made via an official written word document. Attendance & Class Contribution • I will be taking attendance at the start of every class. Do not come up to me after class if you miss the roll call. • For the live sessions, you have 1 excused absence. In other words, you will not be penalized for missing 1 day. Use them wisely! You don’t need to explain why you were absent (although it would be nice to know what’s going on). However, you will be solely responsible for following-up on the material covered in the classes you missed. Of course, this does not mean you can be absent from presentations or exams – you MUST attend all presentation and exams. As per SKKU policy, an absence of 25% of the class will result in an automatic F. • Independently from attendance points, I will occasionally grant contribution points when a student provides insightful comments during class. You can receive up to 2 contribution points for each class. I may or may not notify you of these extra points. • Your participation score for that day, though, will be dropped by 1 point for every unprofessional classroom behavior (including, but not limited to, using your phone or laptop, being rude to the instructor or fellow classmates, failure to actively participate in class exercises, and etc.). I may or may not announce the point deduction on the spot (in order not to break the learning atmosphere of the class). Marketing Team Project (More Information in Marketing Team Project Guideline Document) Students will be grouped into different groups to work with on a marketing plan project. This project will span the entire semester and will involve three parts: a mid-term proposal, a final report, and a final group presentation in class. You will come up with a business plan (i.e. a new product or service or renovating an existing product or service) and apply what you learned in class to develop a strong marketing strategy. v Group Memberships: At the start of the semester, you must answer a quick survey about your group member preference. The survey will ask you how much time you are willing to commit, how much time you expect to commit, and whether there are any friends you want to be grouped together with. If you do not fill out the survey, I will randomly assign you to a group. v Note regarding free riders: Free riders and non-contributors will be SEVERELY punished. Please read the Marketing Project Guidelines for details. Exams The exams will cover everything that was mentioned during lectures (lectures, slides, videos, class discussions, and articles). Make sure to attend the review lecture(s) as important information will be discussed. ACADEMIC DISHONESTY Academically dishonest acts include, but are not limited to: • Cheating • Plagiarism • Unauthorized Collaboration / Collusion • Falsifying Academic Records • Multiple submissions • Use of outside help (e.g. outside paid personnel or AI assistants) • Any other acts (or attempted acts) that violate the basic standard of academic integrity By enrolling in this class you have agreed to observe all student responsibilities and to NOT engage in any kind of academic dishonesty. Students who violate university and course rules about academic honesty will be subject to severe disciplinary penalties. Once there is evidence of academic dishonesty there will be no room for appeals or reassessment. Students caught cheating on the exam will receive an automatic F. If there is sufficient evidence that someone has cheated, the student will receive an F, even if I did not directly observe the behavior. If a student engages in clearly suspicious behavior during the exam, they will be given a warning. If the suspicious behavior continues, the student will be given an F without notification to minimize bothering other hard-working students. MARKETING MANAGEMENT FALL 2026 Class format: Flip Learning Time: M 10:30-11:45 am / W 09:00-10:15 am Wednesday classes will be held live offline. Professor: Jerry Jisang Han E-mail: [비공개 정보 제거] Office Hours: By appointment only: Send me a short email in advance about when you would like to meet and what you would like t
publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: 1) Identify and apply the key tools marketers use to deal with marketing issues. 2) Apply the key principles and use terminology marketers use to discuss marketing issues. 3) Connect the knowledge of marketing to real-world events. 4) Understand the role of marketing in society and in an economic system. 5) Understand the role of marketing in a firm and the relationships between marketing and the other functional areas of business (e.g., accounting, finance, MIS, management). CLASS FORMAT AND POLICIES Class sessions will include lectures, guest speaker talks, discussions of business cases and business press articles, and in class exercises. I expect you to conduct yourselves professionally. You should respect both your classmates and the instructor. This includes arriving to class on time, turning off and putting away your cell phones, refraining from conducting personal conversations, and maintaining a courteous attitude towards your classmates and the instructor. Students who are unruly, unprofessional, or is a negative influence on the class’s learning environment can and will be removed from class with or without warning. GRADING Attendance & Class Contribution 15 % Midterm Proposal Presentation 5 % Midterm Exam 25 % Team Project Report 10 % Team Project Final Presentation 15 % Peer Evaluation -5 ~ 5 % Final Exam 25 % Total 100 % Note: Any questions / appeals in regards to marks or grades must be made within 5 days of it being posted online. For fairness and to root out grade fishing behavior, all appeals should be made via an official written word document. Attendance & Class Contribution • I will be taking attendance at the start of every class. Do not come up to me after class if you miss the roll call. • For the live sessions, you have 1 excused absence. In other words, you will not be penalized for missing 1 day. Use them wisely! You don’t need to explain why you were absent (although it would be nice to know what’s going on). However, you will be solely responsible for following-up on the material covered in the classes you missed. Of course, this does not mean you can be absent from presentations or exams – you MUST attend all presentation and exams. As per SKKU policy, an absence of 25% of the class will result in an automatic F. • Independently from attendance points, I will occasionally grant contribution points when a student provides insightful comments during class. You can receive up to 2 contribution points for each class. I may or may not notify you of these extra points. • Your participation score for that day, though, will be dropped by 1 point for every unprofessional classroom behavior (including, but not limited to, using your phone or laptop, being rude to the instructor or fellow classmates, failure to actively participate in class exercises, and etc.). I may or may not announce the point deduction on the spot (in order not to break the learning atmosphere of the class). Marketing Team Project (More Information in Marketing Team Project Guideline Document) Students will be grouped into different groups to work with on a marketing plan project. This project will span the entire semester and will involve three parts: a mid-term proposal, a final report, and a final group presentation in class. You will come up with a business plan (i.e. a new product or service or renovating an existing product or service) and apply what you learned in class to develop a strong marketing strategy. v Group Memberships: At the start of the semester, you must answer a quick survey about your group member preference. The survey will ask you how much time you are willing to commit, how much time you expect to commit, and whether there are any friends you want to be grouped together with. If you do not fill out the survey, I will randomly assign you to a group. v Note regarding free riders: Free riders and non-contributors will be SEVERELY punished. Please read the Marketing Project Guidelines for details. Exams The exams will cover everything that was mentioned during lectures (lectures, slides, videos, class discussions, and articles). Make sure to attend the review lecture(s) as important information will be discussed. ACADEMIC DISHONESTY Academically dishonest acts include, but are not limited to: • Cheating • Plagiarism • Unauthorized Collaboration / Collusion • Falsifying Academic Records • Multiple submissions • Use of outside help (e.g. outside paid personnel or AI assistants) • Any other acts (or attempted acts) that violate the basic standard of academic integrity By enrolling in this class you have agreed to observe all student responsibilities and to NOT engage in any kind of academic dishonesty. Students who violate university and course rules about academic honesty will be subject to severe disciplinary penalties. Once there is evidence of academic dishonesty there will be no room for appeals or reassessment. Students caught cheating on the exam will receive an automatic F. If there is sufficient evidence that someone has cheated, the student will receive an F, even if I did not directly observe the behavior. If a student engages in clearly suspicious behavior during the exam, they will be given a warning. If the suspicious behavior continues, the student will be given an F without notification to minimize bothering other hard-working students. exactFullPublicAttachmentEducation.educationFullText:
1
Marketing Strategy 
BUS2004, SKK Business School, 2026 Fall 
Instructor: Sungkyun Moon 
 
Class Timing: Mon 13:30 - 14:45 / Wed 12:00 - 13:15 
Classroom: Business Building 33405 
Credit Hours: 3 Credit Hours 
Contact Information:  
Office Hours: 
 Before/After each class 
 In-person or online office hours by appointment 
 
Course Description: The objective of this course is to prepare students for the tasks facing marketing 
managers, who make strategic marketing decisions having a long-term impact on their organization’s 
performance. The course will be particularly useful for students interested in marketing, strategy, 
general management or consulting. The course develops understanding and experience of marketing 
strategy formulation through readings, discussions, a project on competitive marketing strategy and 
case study analysis. For case study analysis, the course uses prominent case study materials such as 
Havard Business School cases. Building on the core marketing courses, this course explores strategic 
topics discussed in the course including identifying appropriate ways to analyze markets and 
understand consumers, gaining market/consumer insights, constructing sustainable competitive 
strategies, strategic branding, strategic new product introduction, CRM, and resource allocation 
strategies. 
Students will learn relevant strategic marketing concepts/theoretical frameworks and apply them to real 
business contexts through conducting case study analysis to analyze strategic and tactical decisions in a 
competitive marketing environment. 
 
Textbooks: 
 Slides and Lecture Notes 
 Case Materials/Assigned Readings 
 Additional readings may be assigned at the discretion of the instructor.  
 
Course Learning Goals: The content-related learning goals of this course are:  
 To understand the overall marketing strategy formulation process. 
 To provide experience in formulating and evaluating marketing strategies in a dynamic 
environment through case study analysis. Case study analysis emulates real business contexts 
and offers the opportunity for students to identify marketing problems and developing 
potential solutions from a managerial perspective. 
 To identify appropriate ways to gain market/consumer insights by analyzing relevant 
information gathered through research. 
 
 2
 To analyze information about consumers, companies, competition and the environment to craft 
appropriate positioning strategies. 
 To analyze firms' marketing strategies, make recommendations to create and/or retain and/or 
enhance competitive advantage.  
 To understand the importance of managing long term relationships with customers/consumers. 
 To evaluate marketing success and performance by linking marketing to finance and 
accounting. 
 
Course Assignments: Several types of assignments have been chosen to achieve the learning goals of 
this course. For successful completion of this course, it is required that students complete all of them. 
Grading rubrics for assignments will be provided later in class.  
 
Case Study Analysis: This is a group assignment. Each student team will be responsible of analyzing 
the marketing case study, answering questions, and providing a written report as a deliverable. The 
instructions/guidelines will be provided as separate documents. Please note that students will be 
randomly assigned to a group, and group information will be announced in i-campus by Week 3. 
 
Marketing Strategy Case Project: This is another group project. This assignment is intended to provide 
students with an opportunity to apply concepts/frameworks covered in the course to assess marketing 
strategies of firms/brands and make recommendations regarding a “real” brand/product. In this 
assignment, you will analyze a brand/product/firm focusing on its competitive advantage comparing to 
rival brands. You will also analyze whether the brand has been successfully competing against the 
rivals or not, providing reasons for the success (or failure), which will be followed by 
recommendations in terms of gaining competitive advantage.  
 
For the group projects, group members will fill out a Peer Evaluation Form in which they will 
confidentially evaluate the contribution of their colleagues excluding themselves to prevent free riding. 
Individual students’ grades for group assignments will be derived from both a group grade and peer 
evaluation.  
 
Evaluation: Students will be evaluated based on the following items:  
 Attendance and Participation: 20% 
 Marketing Case Study Analysis: 25% 
 Marketing Strategy Case Project: 25% 
 Final Exam 30% 
 
Class Policies:  
 
Participation: Participation in this course is defined as broadly as possible. It includes not only in-class 
attendance, behavior and participation, but also several other things such as active cooperation to 
teamwork and excellence in assignments. Class participation provides students with the opportunity to 
develop oral communication skills, the capacity to think logically and react quickly under pressure. 
Your participation in teamwork will be evaluated by your team members at the end of the course. Your 
grade on team elements of the course and participation credit will be significantly lowered if there is 
 
 3
any evidence indicating free-riding in peer evaluation. Active participation in the discussions will 
contribute to the participation grade.  
 
Exams: Pop quizzes may be given during the semester. We will have a final exam. The day, time, and 
electronic devices are not allowed during the exam and quizzes, except when allowed by an instructor.  
 
Make-up Exams: No make-up exams will be given unless a student has a strong reason for missing 
the exam and has notified the instructor prior to the scheduled exam. If a student fails to notify me 
prior to the scheduled exam (regardless of the validity of the excuse), or if a student misses the exam 
without a valid excuse, a make-up exam will not be allowed and the student’s grade will be zero. On 
the date of make-up, the student must provide written documentation explaining the reason for missing 
the exam. 
 
Return of Tests and Collection of Assignments: Anyone failing to return a test to me at the end of a test 
will face the prospect of receiving a zero on the test, or worse, if conditions warrant. Assignments will 
be collected on the due date at the beginning of a class session (or should be electronically submitted 
by the due date if an electronic submission is required).  
 
Late Assignments: Late assignments will be penalized. A student will receive 20% deduction from the 
mark he/she receives if the assignment is late but submitted during the same day. Students will receive 
50% deduction if it is more than one day. 
 
Attendance Policy: Each absence will result in 5 percent deduction from the attendance/participation 
points. If a student makes more than 3 unexcused absences, his/her letter grade shall go down by one 
letter grade. For example, if a student’s final grade is an “A” before taking his/her attendance history 
into account, his/her final grade will be a “B” in case the student has four or more unexcused absences. 
Missing more than 25% of class sessions will result in a failure in the course based on university 
the class and send a valid proof to the instructor within a week. If a student is late (or leaves classroom 
early) for class 3 times, it is considered to be equivalent to one absence unless there is a valid excuse. 
 
Plagiarism Statement: Academic dishonesty is unacceptable, and condemned in the strongest possible 
terms. It undermines the bonds of trust and honesty between members of the community and defrauds 
those who may eventually depend upon our knowledge and integrity. Such dishonesty consists of any 
of the following: cheating, fabrication, plagiarism, and facilitating academic dishonesty.  Academic 
dishonesty may be punishable by a range of penalties including failure in the course.

현재2026-2 해당 분반의 자체 전체16주 운영표와 학교 네이티브 수업시각·강의실에 따른 정규 대면 예약입니다. 실제 출석·시험·미확정 보강 시각은 확정하지 않았습니다. 제외 주차 8,15,16는 원문 시험/휴강/보강·자율학습/개별상담 또는 날짜충돌 구간입니다. 학교 공식8/31 시작의 7일 단위 주차 대응은 예약 제외 경계이며 실제 시험 날짜라는 주장이 아닙니다. 사전영상·휴일 온라인 보강·별도 현장/상담/과제 등 미확정 운영조건은 원문 그대로 보존하며 대면 예약으로 생성하지 않습니다.

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
ㅇ 교과목 소개(오리엔테이션)
ㅇ 재무관리 개요
　 ･ 재무관리의 의의, 재무이론의 발전과정
　 ･ 재무관리의 세부분야(기업재무, 투자론, 금융기관론 등)
　 ･ 재무관리의 목표

ㅇ 화폐의 시간가치(Time Value of Money)
　 ･ 현재가치 vs. 미래가치
　 ･ 유동성 선호
ㅇ 확실성 하에서의 소비와 투자의 결정
　 ･ 피셔의 분리정리(Fisher's Separation Theorem)

ㅇ 주식(Stock)
　･ 주식의 기본개념(보통주, 우선주, 유상증자, 무상증자, 배당락 등)
　･ 주식의 가치평가
　　현금흐름할인모형(배당평가모형, 이익평가모형, 잉여현금흐름모형)
　　자산가치평가모형
　　상대가치평가모형(PER모형, PBR모형, PSR모형, EV/EBITDA)
weekly.BIGO: 기업의 가치를 어떻게 평가할 수 있는가?

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
o 채권(Bond)
　 ･ 채권의 기본개념(의의, 기본구조, 종류 등)
　 ･ 채권가격 정리(Malkiel), 채권 수익률 결정요인
　 ･ 이자율 기간구조이론(Term Structure Theory), 이자율 위험구조
　 ･ 듀레이션(Duration), 볼록성(Convexity)
　 ･ 채권면역전략(immunization strategy)
weekly.BIGO: 채권의 가치를 어떻게 평가할 수 있는가?

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
ㅇ 포트폴리오 이론(Portfolio Theory)
　 ･ 기대수익률과 위험, 상관계수/투자비율과 포트폴리오 위험
　 ･ 투자종목 수와 위험분산 효과
　 ･ 위험자산의 효율적 포트폴리오와 최적증권의 선택
ㅇ 자본자산가격결정모형(CAPM: Capital Asset Pricing Model)
　 ･ 위험자산과 무위험자산의 결합
　 ･ 자본시장선(CML)과 증권시장선(SML)
　 ･ 포트폴리오의 베타와 기대수익률

ㅇ 요인모형과 차익거래가격결정모형(APT: Arbitrage Pricing Model)
　 ･ 단일요인모형(Market Model)과 다요인모형
　 ･ 3요인, 4요인, 5요인 모형
ㅇ 자본예산(Capital Budgeting)
　 ･ 회수기간법, 회계적이익률법, 순현가(NPV)법, 내부수익률(IRR)법
ㅇ 위험을 고려한 자본예산
　 ･ WACC, 영업레버리지, 재무레버리지, 이자비용의 감세효과

ㅇ 자본구조이론(Capital Structure Theory)
　 ･ MM이전의 자본구조이론(NI 접근법, NOI 접근법, 전통적 접근법)
　 ･ MM의 자본구조이론(무관련이론(MM58), 수정이론(MM63))
　 ･ Miller의 균형부채이론, 파산비용과 자본구조, 대리인비용과자본구조, 정보비대칭과 신호이론(Signaling Theory), 자금조달순위이론(Pecking Order Theory)

ㅇ 배당정책 이론(Dividend Policy Theory)
　 ･ 배당정책의 개념, 배당의 척도, 배당소득과 기업가치
　 ･ MM의 배당이론(무관련이론), 자가배당
　 ･ 세금과 배당, 배당의 고객효과, 거래비용과 배당, 대리인비용, 정보비대칭, 불확실성과 배당
　 ･ 배당수준의 결졍요인, 안정배당정책
　 ･ 주식배당, 주식분할과 주식병합, 자사주 매입
ㅇ 합병(M&A)
　 ･ 합병의 종류 및 방법
　 ･ 합병 방어전략(White Knight, Crown Jewel, Green Mail, Poison Pill, Golden Parachutes)
　 ･ 합병의 동기(시너지효과 가설, 신호가설, 세금효과 가설, 대리인 가설 등)

ㅇ 선물(Futures)
　 ･ 선물거래의 동기, 기능, 메커니즘 및 특징
　 ･ 보유비용 모형(Cost of Carry Model)
　 ･ 선물가격과 기대현물가격(Contango, Backwardation)
　 ･ 베이시스(Basis), 스프레드(Spread)
　 ･ 헤지거래(hedge), 차익거래(arbitrage), 투기거래(speculation)
　 ･ 상품선물(농축산물선물, 금속선물, 에너지선물 등)
　 ･ 금융선물(주가지수선물, 금리선물, 통화선물 등)

ㅇ 옵션(Options)
　 ･ 옵션의 개요, 종류 및 기능
　 ･ 스프레드 전략(스트래들, 스트랭글, 비율 스프레드, 캘린더 스프레드, 버터플라이 등)
　 ･ 합성전략 및 헤징전략(Covered Call, Protective Put)
　 ･ 옵션가격에 영향을 미치는 요인
　 ･ 풋-콜 패리티(Put-Call Parity), 옵션가격결정모형
　 ･ 내재변동성(Implied Volatility), 옵션 민감도(Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho)
　 ･ 이색옵션(Exotic Option)
　 ･ 옵션의 응용(주주/채권자 입장에서의 기업가치, CB, BW, EB 등)
weekly.BIGO: 옵션 프리미엄에 영향을 미치는 요인은 무엇인가?

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
ㅇ 스왑(Swap)
　 ･ 스왑의 역사, 거래목적 및 종류
　 ･ 이자율스왑(IRS), 통화스왑(CRS), 자산스왑 등
ㅇ VaR(Value at Risk)
　 ･ 비모수적 방법과 모수적 방법
　 ･ 주식과 채권의 VaR
　 ･ 스트레스 테스트(Stress Test), 사후검증(Back Testing)
　 ･ VaR의 용도 및 한계
weekly.BIGO: VaR을 통해 위험을 어떻게 측정할 수 있는가?

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
ㅇ 국제재무관리
　 ･ 외환시장, 환율제도, 환율의 표시방법, 환율의 종류
　 ･ 외환거래(현물환거래, 선물환거래, FX Swap거래, NDF거래 등)
　 ･ 환율결정이론(PPP, 피셔효과, 국제피셔효과, IRPT)
　 ･ 환위험 관리(대내적 관리기법, 대외적 관리기법)
　 ･ 국제금융시장(유로통화시장, 외국채시장, 유로본드시장 등)

ㅇ 정보비대칭과 시장효울성
　 ･ 정보비대칭과 시장실패: 레몬시장 이론(Lemon Market Theory)
　 ･ 효율적 시장가설(Efficient Market Hypothesis: EMH):
약형, 준강형, 강형
　 ･ EMH의 검증과 시장 이례현상(Market Anomaly)
ㅇ 행태재무학(Behavioral Finance)
　 ･ 행태재무학적 비판

weekly.BIGO: 휴일 또는 교강사의 사정으로 휴강이 발생할 경우 보강 진행

detail.CLASS_INFO:
본 강의는 플립러닝(Flipped Learning) 방식으로 진행합니다.  
월요일 강의는 교수자가 강의 영상을 사전에 만들어 아이캠퍼스에 업로드하면 학습자가 영상으로 공부하고 수요일에는 학생들끼리 팀을 이루어 해당 주제에 대해 함께 논의합니다. 
또한, 토론에 앞서 교수자가  핵심 내용을 10-20분 내외로 추가 설명해 드립니다. 
조직행동은  흥미로운 주제들이 가득한 과목으로 서로의 아이디어와 시각을 나누는 시간으로 부담 없이 참여하면 됩니다.

플립러닝의 주요 강점은 다음과 같습니다.
1)학습자 중심의 자기 주도 학습
2)수업 시간의 효율적 활용
3)사고 능력 배양
4)즉각적인 피드백
detail.BIGO: 출석, 토론, 개인 과제(리포트), 중간/기말시험, 팀 발표 등 평가요소를 반영한 절대평가 입니다.

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
CH.1 An Overview of Organizational Behavior - 조직행동 소개
CH.2 Environmental Change - 조직이 속한 환경 변화 이해
weekly.BIGO:
-조직행동을 공부해야 하는 이유
-조직이 속한 외부 환경 변화

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.3 Individual Characteristics - 성격, 지능 등
weekly.BIGO:
-개인의 성격 특성을 설명하는 주요 이론 학습:  
  Big Five, Locus of Control 등

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.4 Individual values, Perceptions, and Reactions I - 개인의 태도, 가치관 등
weekly.BIGO:
-태도의 형성과정, 인지부조화, 정서 등
-직무에 대한 주요한 태도

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.4 Individual Values, Perceptions, and Reactions II - 지각, 귀인이론 등
weekly.BIGO:
-지각의 정의 및 과정, 지각에 관한 주요 이론 
-스트레스가 개인과 조직에 미치는 영향

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.5 Motivating Behavior I - 동기란 무엇인가
weekly.BIGO:
-인간의 니즈로 동기를 설명하는 주요 이론:
  Maslow 5단계 욕구이론 등

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.6 Motivating Behavior with work and rewards - 일과 보상을 통한 동기부여

weekly.BIGO:
-커뮤니케이션 과정, 유형 및 방해요인 등 이해
-커뮤니케이션 특성 진단 및 결과 토의
-지난 7주 동안 학습한 내용을 리뷰하는 시험 진행

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT: CH.7 Groups and Teams - 그룹과 팀
weekly.BIGO:
-그룹과 팀의 공통점 및 차이점 이해
-실제 조직 사례 공유

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
CH.11 Traditional Leadership Approach - 초기 리더십
CH.12 Contemporary Views of Leadership in Organization - 현대 리더십
CH.8 Decision Making and Problem Solving - 의사결정과 문제해결
weekly.BIGO: -의사결정 과정의 이해와 의사결정 행동을 설명하는 주요 이론 학습

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
CH.10 Conflict and Negotiation in Organization - 갈등과 협상
CH.13 Power, Influence, and Politics - 권력과 정치
weekly.BIGO:
-갈등의 본질과 협상을 통한 효과적인 해결방안 
-조직 내 권력과 정치의 이해
-리더십 등 흥미로운 주제를 선정하여 팀 별 사례 발표
학생 상담 및 기타 학생들에게 도움이 되는 활동 예정

weekly.PLAN_WEEK_CONT:
CH.15 Organizational Culture - 조직 문화
CH.16 Organizational Change and Change Management - 조직 변화 및 변화 관리
weekly.BIGO:
-조직문화의 중요성과 형성과정 이해
-조직변화를 위한 변화관리 및 조직개발 숙지
중간시험 이후 학습한 내용을 최종 점검하는 시험

수강 대상: 경영학과
선수과목: 회계원리
수업 비고: 1회 결석은 1점씩 감점(5회 이상 결석시 학칙에 의거 F처리). 직계존비속의 결혼식과 장례, 병역의무관련 사항, 생리공결, 전염병 등 인정되는 사유 외의 개인적인 사유로 인한 결석은 결석으로 처리.
과제는 교과서 연습문제(4회 예정). 과제는 늦게 제출시 1점 감점, 성실하게 작성하여 제출만 하면 만점으로 처리. 연습장 등에 직접 손으로 작성하여 제출할 것
시험의 총점을 25% 이상 취득하지 못하면 F 처리함.
시험은 OX문항(5~10문항), 객관식(20문항), 주관식 단답형(5~6문항), 주관식 약술형 등으로 구성. 
평가항목 중 기타는 수업태도에 해당. 수업태도가 불량할 경우(예: 핸드폰 사용, 수업 도중 강의실 출입) 별도 고지없이 수시로 감점되며 감점에는 하한이 없음.
공식 학기 기간과 휴업일을 적용한 대면 수업 날짜입니다. 실제 별도 보강은 학교 공지를 확인하세요.

교수의 현장 지명에 의해 랜덤하게 발표조를 정함 · (토론 채점 기준; 원칙적으로 교수 발표 지명이 있을 때 빠짐 없이 발표만 하면 A 이상 등급 가능; 모든 조에 동등한 발표기회 제공) - A+/A: 조는 지명된 경우 모든 발표에 참여했다 (A+: 해당 주 사례 발표 중 가장 우수한 발표의 경우) - B+: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했지만 내용은 평균 이상인 경우 - B: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했고 내용은 평균 이하 수준 - C: 조는 지명된 발표에 3~4회 불참했다 - D: 지명된 조 발표를 5회 이상 안 하는 경우 - F: 교수 지명이 있었음에도 불구하고 모든 경우에 조 발표를 안 하였거나 토론시간 중 토론 자체를 하지 않는 등 불성실한 조별 활동이 이루어진 경우 · 등급별 점수 환산 (절대평가): A+ = 15점; publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: 1) Uber versus Didi: The Race for China’s Ride-hailing Industry (Harvard) (사례 2) Walmart: Navigating a Changing Retail Landscape, 2019 (Harvard) (사례 3) Circle: Reinventing the Future of Finance (Harvard) (사례 4) Enel: The Future of Energy (Harvard) 사례 구매 하버드 사례 패키지 구매링크는 수강확정 후 공지 (구매필수. 미구매시 기말 총점 100점 만점에서 1점 감점) 성적 산정 중간고사 (없음), 기말고사 (50%), 사례퀴즈 (20%), 사례토론발표 - 조별 (20%), 강의출석 (10%) 성적평가 방식 절대평가 수업 일정 2026년 9월 1일 ~ 12월 15일 (총 16주차, 기말고사 12/15 포함) 2. 과제 내용 사례퀴즈 (개인, 20%) · (목적) 글로벌 기업 사례 연구를 통한 경영전략에 대한 실무현실적 이해 증대 · (형식) 총 4회에 걸쳐 사례를 사전학습하고 객관식 또는 OX 문항으로 답하는 퀴즈 형식 (사례 내용 자체에서 출제). 퀴즈는 모두 화요일 오프라인 수업 중에 실시합니다. · (사례와 시험 일시는 아래 주차별 어젠다 참조) · (평가) 사례별 각 10점 만점, 4회 시험결과 중 가장 낮은 점수를 제외한 3회 성적 기준으로 산정 (Drop the Lowest); 교수의 현장 지명에 의해 랜덤하게 발표조를 정함 · (토론 채점 기준; 원칙적으로 교수 발표 지명이 있을 때 빠짐 없이 발표만 하면 A 이상 등급 가능; 모든 조에 동등한 발표기회 제공) - A+/A: 조는 지명된 경우 모든 발표에 참여했다 (A+: 해당 주 사례 발표 중 가장 우수한 발표의 경우) - B+: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했지만 내용은 평균 이상인 경우 - B: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했고 내용은 평균 이하 수준 - C: 조는 지명된 발표에 3~4회 불참했다 - D: 지명된 조 발표를 5회 이상 안 하는 경우 - F: 교수 지명이 있었음에도 불구하고 모든 경우에 조 발표를 안 하였거나 토론시간 중 토론 자체를 하지 않는 등 불성실한 조별 활동이 이루어진 경우 · 등급별 점수 환산 (절대평가): A+ = 15점; 교수의 현장 지명에 의해 랜덤하게 발표조를 정함 · (토론 채점 기준; 원칙적으로 교수 발표 지명이 있을 때 빠짐 없이 발표만 하면 A 이상 등급 가능; 모든 조에 동등한 발표기회 제공) - A+/A: 조는 지명된 경우 모든 발표에 참여했다 (A+: 해당 주 사례 발표 중 가장 우수한 발표의 경우) - B+: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했지만 내용은 평균 이상인 경우 - B: 조는 지명된 발표에 1~2회 불참했고 내용은 평균 이하 수준 - C: 조는 지명된 발표에 3~4회 불참했다 - D: 지명된 조 발표를 5회 이상 안 하는 경우 - F: 교수 지명이 있었음에도 불구하고 모든 경우에 조 발표를 안 하였거나 토론시간 중 토론 자체를 하지 않는 등 불성실한 조별 활동이 이루어진 경우 · 등급별 점수 환산 (절대평가): A+ = 15점; A = 14점; B+ = 13점; B = 12점; C = 10점; D = 8점; F = 6점 (15점 만점) · (총점 합산) 20점 = 조별 발표점수 15점 + 조원평가점수 5점 (아래 양식 참고) 중간고사 · 별도 중간고사 없음 (8주차 중간고사 기간에는 시험 및 수업 없음) 기말고사 (50%) · 일정 - 12/15 (화) 수업시간 중 · 시험 방식 - 오프라인 객관식 (OMR) · 시험 범위 - 강의 전체(오프라인 수업 및 온라인 콘텐츠 포함)와 사례 모두 포함 강의참여 (10%) · (구성) 출석 5점 + 수업 참여 5점 = 총 10점 · (출석규정) 수강률 × 10점 = 수강률 점수 (예시: 90% 수강 = 10점 × 0.9 = 9점). 화요일 오프라인 출석과 목요일 온라인 콘텐츠 시청 이력을 합산하여 수강률을 산정합니다. · (지각 및 불출석 규정) 5분 이후 출석 경우 지각; 지각 1회당 0.2점 감점; 질환 또는 교수가 인정하는 사고에 한해 결석 인정 · 출석은 모바일시스템 체크인으로만 인정 (구두 출석확인은 인정 불가). 온라인 수업은 아이캠퍼스 진도율 100% 도달 시 출석 인정 · (수업 중 참여 5점) 활발한 발표와 토론을 통한 경영자 역량강화를 위하여 수업 중 토론 우수자에 대한 가점 부여 · 우수한 수업 중 발표: 5점 (전체 인원의 10% 수준), 평균 수준 참여: 4점 (전체 중 80% 수준), 참여 부족: 3점 (전체 중 10% 수준) 3. 주차별 어젠다 강의일은 화요일 오프라인 1회이며, 목요일은 온라인 강의로 대체하여 운영합니다. 사례퀴즈 4회는 모두 화요일 오프라인 수업 중에 실시합니다 (5주차, 7주차, 11주차, 15주차). 비사례 주차의 팀 워크숍 주제는 사전 공유하지 않으며, 수업 진행 상황에 맞춰 해당 수업 중에 공지합니다. 주차 형식 일자 주제 및 팀 활동 사례 / 퀴즈 · 비고 1 오프라인 9/1 (화) 강의소개 · 조편성 · 전략은 무엇인가? 사례학습 방법 오리엔테이션 [팀 플레이] 조별 워크숍 — 주제는 수업 진행에 맞춰 공지 사례 없음 사례 패키지 구매 안내 온라인 9/3 (목) 전략은 무엇인가? exactOriginalEducation.educationFullText:
강의계획서







강의 일정(안)
* 강의 일정 및 수업 시간에 다루는 내용은 상황에 따라 변경될 수 있음 


수업 방식
본 수업은 사전제작 온라인 수업입니다. 사전에 녹화된 강의 영상을 수강생이 자율적으로 학습하는 형태로 진행됩니다. 

I-campus 
강의 관련 공지사항, 강의자료 및 학습 자료는 i-Campus 내 강의 커뮤니티를 통해 제공될 예정입니다. 모든 수강생께서는 i-Campus 강의 커뮤니티에 정상적으로 가입되어 있는지 확인하시고, 강의 진행에 차질이 없도록 주기적으로 접속하여 공지사항과 자료를 확인해 주시기 바랍니다.

학점 

출석 및 평소 학습태도 (200점)


한 주차에 여러 개의 온라인 강의 영상이 업로드된 경우, 해당 주차의 모든 영상을 수강해야 출석으로 인정됩니다. 일부 영상만 수강한 경우 지각으로 처리됩니다. 
본 수업은 사전 제작된 온라인 강의를 충분한 기간 동안 자유롭게 수강할 수 있도록 운영됩니다. 따라서 지각 또는 결석에 대해 불가피한 사유(개인 사정, 질병, 일정 중복 등)를 이유로 한 예외 인정은 하지 않습니다.
출석은 2~7주차 및 9~14주차에 확인합니다. 1주차, 8주차, 15주차는 별도의 출석 확인을 실시하지 않습니다. 총 12회의 출석을 평가하며, 출석 점수의 원점수는 최대 240점​입니다.
출석점수 (원점수) 200~240점 → 최종 출석점수 200점(만점)으로 반영
출석점수 (원점수) 160~199점 → 취득한 점수를 그대로 최종 출석점수로 반영
출석점수 (원점수) 0~159점 → F 학점 부여






2) 퀴즈 (200점) 
2~7주차 및 9~14주차 온라인 강의 영상을 모두 수강한 후에는 해당 주차의 퀴즈에 응시해야 합니다. 퀴즈는 해당 주차 토요일 23:59까지 완료한 경우에만 퀴즈에서 획득한 점수만큼 인정됩니다. 마감 이후 7일 이내에 제출한 경우에는 획득 점수의 50%만 반영되며, 그 이후에는 응시하더라도 0점으로 처리됩니다.
퀴즈는 총 12회 실시하며, 이 중 ​점수가 높은 10회의 점수만 최종 성적에 반영됩니다. (10회 × 20점 = 200점)
각 퀴즈는 1회만 응시할 수 있으며, 퀴즈를 시작한 시점부터 20분 이내에 완료해야 합니다.
퀴즈 문항은 온라인 강의 내용을 성실히 학습한 학생이라면 충분히 해결할 수 있는 수준으로 출제됩니다.
퀴즈 응시 시 교재, 강의자료, 인터넷 등 참고자료를 활용하는 것은 허용​됩니다. 다만, 타 학생과 문제를 상의하거나 답안을 공유하는 등 협업하여 응시하는 행위는 허용되지 않으며, 적발 시 학칙에 따라 부정행위로 처리될 수 있습니다.

3) 중간고사 및 기말고사 (각 300점)
중간고사와 기말고사 일정은 다음과 같습니다. 
중간고사: 8주차 10월 20일 화요일 오전 10:30~11:30
기말고사: 15주차 12월 8일 화요일 오전 10:30~11:30
중간고사와 기말고사는 반드시 지정된 강의실에 출석하여 i-Campus에 접속한 후 응시하여야 합니다.
노트북을 이용하여 시험을 진행하므로, 시험 당일에는 반드시 정상적으로 작동하는 노트북과 충전기를 지참하시기 바랍니다.
시험은 Closed Book 방식으로 진행됩니다. 
중간고사에 응시하지 않을 경우 중간고사 성적은 0점으로 처리됩니다.
기말고사에 응시하지 않을 경우에는 학칙에 따라 해당 교과목의 최종 성적은 F로 처리됩니다.
중간고사 및 기말고사에 대한 추가시험(대체시험)은 원칙적으로 실시하지 않습니다. 
시험 강의실 등에 대한 세부 내용은 시험 1주 전에 공지사항을 통해 다시 안내하겠습니다.

* 학점 예상 분포 (확정은 아님)
- 상위합계 점수 950점 이상 (A+)
- 합계 점수 900점 이상 (A)
- 합계 점수 850점 이상 (B+)
- 합계 점수 800점 이상 (B)
- 합계 점수 600점 이상 (C+)
- 합계 점수 600점 미만 (C이하) (400점 미만일시 F)
* 단, 상대평가가 적용될 경우 학점이 일부 조정될 수 있음. 예를 들어 많은 학생이 아주 우수한 성적을 거두었다면, A학점을 받기 위해서 920점 이상을 획득해야 할 수도 있음.


기타 
출석, 퀴즈, 시험 등에서 부정 행위가 발각될 경우, 모든 관련 당사자들은 엄격하게 F 학점으로 처리하겠습니다. 
이해가 되지 않은 내용이 있을 경우 적극적으로 질문해 주세요. 본인이 이해가 되지 않은 경우, 다른 사람도 이해가 되지 않는 경우가 많으므로, 질문을 함으로써 다 같이 배울 수 있는 좋은 기회가 될 수 있습니다. 강의게시판을 통해 질문을 올리거나, 수강생들끼리 질문 및 답변을 주고받을 것을 적극 권장합니다. 
강의에 대한 요청사항이 있거나, 질문이 있는 경우, 혹은 개인적인 상담이 필요한 경우 부담 갖지 말고 언제든지 연락주세요. 


여러분을 만나게 되어 정말 반갑습니다.
한 학기 동안 즐거운 시간을 보낼 수 있길 바랍니다.

publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: Course Description This course has two central themes: (1) How to think systematically and strategically about aspects of managing people in the organizational context (or human resources [HR]), and (2) What needs to be done to implement these policies and to achieve competitive advantage through people. With the basic premise that both organizations and workers can thrive together, this course will focus on the roles of formal and informal organizational policies and practices. Formal policies include recruitment, selection, rewards, and performance management. Informal policies include culture, communication, and leadership. Throughout the course, we will discuss how those formal and informal policies can be developed and implemented effectively, that is, in a way that benefits both employers and employees. Course Objectives At the conclusion of the course, students should be able to: • Clearly communicate the value that effective HR policies/practices, • Identify and explain foundational HR concepts and policies/practices, • Analyze and critique an organization’s HR policies/practices, • Recommend HR policies/practices that support business strategy and goals. Course Materials Readings, assignments, and cases will be used to highlight issues and problems that face organizations as they manage people in the organizations. The readings consist of a mix of news articles, reports, practitioner articles (e.g., Harvard Business Review), academic articles, book chapters, and others like videos and podcasts. Please purchase the Harvard Business School case Coursepak. The link to the Coursepak will be provided via icampus. Assignments and Grading Your grade in this class will be based on your performance on the following assignments: Assignments Responsibility Weight Due date Class Participation Individual 20% Reflection Paper Individual 20% Before the case classes (see the course schedule) Quizzes (4) Individual 20% See the course schedule Hot Topic Paper Team 20% Midnight, 10/20 (Tue) Live Case Analysis Paper & Presentation Team 20% Midnight, 12/2 (Wed) 2 SungKyunKwan University BUS3054 Class Participation. Class activities will be based on the assumption that students are familiar with the course materials. Therefore, you should be prepared for class and will be called upon to discuss assigned materials. Your Class Participation score will be determined by your (a) class attendance and (b) my assessment of your total contribution to the learning environment. • Class attendance is required; you cannot participate if you are absent. Attendance consists of watching the Tuesday lecture online on time (i.e., before the Thursday class). SKKU policies indicate that students who fail to achieve 75 percent of the attendance credits should get an F as a final grade. Class Participation score for missed classes will be zero for that day. Please e-mail me if you know you are going to be absent – this will enable me to score your participation as “not present” rather than “not participating.” • Contributions to the learning environment can come in many forms – making observations, answering questions, summarizing other’s views, commenting on other students' comments, or debating the instructor's view. It is the quality of your contribution, not the quantity that matters. Examples of quality contribution include: moving the conversation forward, offering an alternative view that peers had not considered, provoking deeper thinking. Reflection Paper. Reflection paper is a short response to one of assigned questions in an assigned case reading (e.g., Harvard Business School case). This assignment is graded on a PASS/FAIL basis. The purpose of this assignment is to facilitate the class discussion, therefore no feedback will be provided. If you would like feedback on your response paper, please ask me via email. • Submit a reflection paper the day before a case discussion day. For example, if a case discussion is scheduled for Thursday, submit a reflection paper by midnight on Wednesday. • Reflection paper’s format is typically, ½ a page and definitely no longer than 1 page. 12-point font, double-spaced, 1-inch margins. Be sure to include your name and number all pages (if longer than one page). Quizzes. There will be several quizzes throughout the semester. I want to emphasize that the goal of quizzes is to re-emphasize key points that we discuss in class, not to trip you up on small details. Therefore, there will be no trick questions. If you’ve attended classes and done a quick review of the slides, I anticipate that you will find the quizzes fairly easy to complete. Hot Topic Paper. Your team is to prepare a paper on one specific “hot topic” related to HR. You will need to provide an overview of the issue, why it is “hot,” and what we know and do not yet know about the issue. For this, please do the following: • Choose an article from a magazine (e.g. Harvard Business Review, Time, Economist, Business Week, or Forbes) or a newspaper (e.g. New York Times or Wall Street Journal) printed anytime since January 1, 2019. The article should be related to HR. • Analyze the contents as they apply to the course. For this exercise try to answer the following questions: Why is the article important? What makes it current? What are the debatable issues? What are the potential HR policy implications for managers (get creative in your suggestions). I would strongly encourage you to research and find related articles (in newspapers or research via library databases) and include these as evidence in your answers (not those already included in the course material). Of course, you will be turning in a copy of the article as well. • Example: (1) How would AI affect HR? (2) How the “gig economy” or “platform economy” changes the way organizations manage people? (3) Is “remote work” here to stay? (4) How would generation issues affect HR? • Hot Topic Paper’s format is maximum 8-pages, 12-point font, double-spaced, 1-inch margins. Title, tables and/or figures do not count toward your page limit. Be sure to include your team 3 SungKyunKwan University BUS3054 members’ names and number all pages. Live Case Analysis Paper. Conduct interviews (e.g., owners, executives, HR managers), learn about a company’s HR policies and practices, and make your team’s own recommendations to the company. The purpose of this assignment is to demonstrate the ability to build an HR solution based on sound logic, and to sell your solution in a convincing and influential manner. The company of your choice should be with a single line of business, business unit, or franchise employing 15 or more people. As an outside consultant, you want management to buy-in to your analysis; you want to make a strong business case. Therefore, be sure that your analysis touches on the following at some point: • Business Summary o Using information collected from at least one face-to-face meeting, describe: o The company overview (e.g., number of employees, number of jobs, location, main products/services, main competitors) o The company’s business strategy – (a) “why do customers buy the products/services of this company, instead of competitors (i.e., customer value proposition)?” and (b) “what do the company excel at to deliver the customer value proposition?” • The company’s culture and HR policies/practices o How would you describe the company’s culture? o How does the company’s culture affect company’s strategy execution? Does it contribute or impede the strategy execution? Why? o What are the formal/informal HR policies/practices that determine the culture? • Recommendations o Given what you have documented, recommend what HR solutions your team will recommend to align the HR practices with the company’s strategic approach. Make your recommendations realistic by considering the company’s resource constraints (e.g., financial resources, time urgency, unions, government regulations). Team Peer Rating. Students are expected to contribute dutifully to the work of the group on these assignments. Accordingly, at the end of the module, each student will provide a confidential evaluation of the other members of her/his team. Peer ratings will be strictly confidential. Course Policies Late work. I am providing all students with a 3-day late assignment bank. This means that you can submit any one assignment up to 3 days after the deadline without any penalty or need for an explanation. Alternatively, you can submit three different assignments, each one day after the deadline, without any penalty or need for an explanation, etc. My hope is that this relieves stress due to unforeseen circumstances and/or conflicts with other course deadlines. Work submitted late (and after you have used up your bank) will still be accepted but will receive a reduced grade (unless we have agreed to an exception ahead of time). Re-grading. If you request to have something regraded, your score may increase, decrease or stay the same. In most cases, grades will not be adjusted, as all grades are carefully considered and reviewed by the instructor. Academic accommodations. I am available to discuss appropriate academic accommodations for students with disabilities. 4 SungKyunKwan University BUS3054 Honesty and integrity. The purpose of this assignment is to demonstrate the ability to build an HR solution based on sound logic, and to sell your solution in a convincing and influential manner. The company of your choice should be with a single line of business, business unit, or franchise employing 15 or more people. Does it contribute or impede the strategy execution? Why? o What are the formal/informal HR policies/practices that determine the culture? • Recommendations o Given what you have documented, recommend what HR solutions your team will recommend to align the HR practices with the company’s strategic approach. Therefore, be sure that your analysis touches on the following at some point: • Business Summary o Using information collected from at least one face-to-face meeting, describe: o The company overview (e.g., number of employees, number of jobs, location, main products/services, main competitors) o The company’s business strategy – (a) “why do customers buy the products/services of this company, instead of competitors (i.e., customer value proposition)?” and (b) “what do the company excel at to deliver the customer value proposition?” • The company’s culture and HR policies/practices o How would you describe the company’s culture? o How does the company’s culture affect company’s strategy execution? Does it contribute or impede the strategy execution? Why? o What are the formal/informal HR policies/practices that determine the culture? • Recommendations o Given what you have documented, recommend what HR solutions your team will recommend to align the HR practices with the company’s strategic approach. Make your recommendations realistic by considering the company’s resource constraints (e.g., financial resources, time urgency, unions, government regulations). Team Peer Rating. Students are expected to contribute dutifully to the work of the group on these assignments. Accordingly, at the end of the module, each student will provide a confidential evaluation of the other members of her/his team. Peer ratings will be strictly confidential. Course Policies Late work. I am providing all students with a 3-day late assignment bank. This means that you can submit any one assignment up to 3 days after the deadline without any penalty or need for an explanation. Alternatively, you can submit three different assignments, each one day after the deadline, without any penalty or need for an explanation, etc. My hope is that this relieves stress due to unforeseen circumstances and/or conflicts with other course deadlines. Work submitted late (and after you have used up your bank) will still be accepted but will receive a reduced grade (unless we have agreed to an exception ahead of time). Re-grading. If you request to have something regraded, your score may increase, decrease or stay the same. In most cases, grades will not be adjusted, as all grades are carefully considered and reviewed by the instructor. Academic accommodations. I am available to discuss appropriate academic accommodations for students with disabilities. 4 SungKyunKwan University BUS3054 Honesty and integrity. In any course at the SKK University, personal ethics should be an issue of great significance. This means that there is no deception in your representation of what you think or the work you submit. This class prohibits all forms of academic cheating and plagiarism. These are a breach of conduct, and students are subject to disciplinary actions. In addition, students are bound by the following specific guidelines for all work completed in this course. • Individual work is to be completed without the assistance of others. • Assignments identified as team-based work are to be completed by only members of the team. • While group interaction is encouraged when studying, any work submitted under your name must be your own work. • All the deliverables submitted in this class should be an original work of the student. Plagiarism in any form, including the use of previous years’ materials or the submission for other classes will not be accepted. • Written deliverables must use appropriate citations to signify when arguments or analyses rely on the ideas or insights of others, including any of the readings in the course materials. • Any use in class assignments of case analyses or any other material in any format from any course taught at any time in the past or present will be considered a violation of the Honor Code. • Unless specific permission is granted to the entire class, when preparing a case, confine your analysis to the facts of the case, using your common sense and deductive reasoning to draw conclusions from the facts and information presented. • If you use ideas that are not your own, they must be cited and/or referenced. 5 SungKyunKwan University BUS3054 Course Schedule (subject to change) *Readings can be found on the iCampus website (icampus.skku.edu). 교과목목표 1. 학생들이 융합을 통해 사회적·예술적 가치를 창출하고 창의력, PBL(Problem/Project Based Learning) 기반의 문제 해결 능력 및 팀 프로젝트 수행 능력을 기른다. 2. ‘지역(종로구) 연계 프로젝트’를 통해 대학과 지역의 동반 성장 모델을 모색·경험하며, 지역 중심 시대에 요구되는 혁신 역량을 기른다.  3. 지역사회가 가진 현안에 대한 탐색과 해결 과정을 통해, 지역 공동체에 대한 공적 책임 의식과 바람직한 태도를 함양한다.   4. 지역사회와의 연대를 통해 지역 문화 활성화에 기여한다.수   업   내   용 참고1주차 오리엔테이션2주차 조 편성, 아이스브레이킹, 브레인스토밍3주차 종로구의 지역적 특성과 문화예술 현황 및 이슈 자료 조사 및 아이템 구체화, 팀별 신청서 작성전문가 특강(종로문화재단)팀별 신청서 제출4주차 법정 공휴일(추석 연휴, 9/24)5주차 자료 조사 및 아이템 구체화, 아이템 확정, 과제 신청서 초안 작성과제 신청서 초안 제출6주차 과제 신청서 작성 과제 신청서 최종 제출7주차 중간 발표8주차 프로토타입 설계 9주차 프로토타입 설계10주차 프로토타입 제작11주차 프로토타입 제작 (프로젝트 결과물 1차 완성) 12주차 프로토타입 수정13주차 프로토타입 완성 (프로젝트 결과물 2차 완성) 14주차 최종 검토 및 수정(결과보고서 포함) 결과보고서 초안 제출15주차 최종 검토 및 수정(결과보고서 포함) 결과보고서 최종 제출16주차 기말 발표과제물 팀별 신청서, 과제 신청서(예산안 포함), 결과보고서, 정산 서류 (지정 서식에 맞춰 한글(HWP) 및 엑셀(XLSX) 문서로 작성) 프로젝트 결과물평가요소출석참여중간기말기타(자기/동료평가)합계20%20%20%30%10%100%
평가방법
 * 출석: 결석 –4점, 지각 –2점 (공결 및 병결 합산 1회 인정, 단 예비군 훈련 예외) * 수업 시간과 조 활동에 적극적으로 참여하는 것이 중요합니다.  * ‘중간’ 점수는 중간 발표와 제출물(과제 신청서(예산안 포함) 등)을 합산해 결정합니다. * ‘기말’ 점수는 기말 발표와 제출물(결과보고서, 프로젝트 결과물, 정산 서류 등)을 합산해 결정합니다. 프로젝트 결과물의 평가는 완성도와 구현성이 주요 기준입니다. * 모든 ‘제출 양식’은 지정된 서식과 기한을 준수해야 하며, 이를 지키지 않을 경우 감점이 있을 수 있습니다.
 * ‘자기/동료평가’는 별도의 양식이 제공됩니다. 프로젝트 기여에 관한 간략한 설문조사입니다.

publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: Course Description The discipline of accounting and the work of accountants are introduced in two courses, Introduction to Financial Accounting (GBA 2003) and Introduction to Managerial Accounting (GBA 2004). Elements of financial accounting are covered in the first course as they relate to the preparation and use of accounting reports for business entities, emphasizing accounting as a provider of financial information for external reporting purposes. Elements of managerial accounting are covered in the second course as they relate to the internal use of accounting information in making business decisions and controlling business operations. II. Learning Outcomes Upon completion of this course you should be able to demonstrate the following; (1) Describe the basic financial statements, their nature, purposes and use by decision makers; (2) Define and/or apply general accounting terms, concepts and processes; (3) Record basic transactions and analyze their impact on the financial statements of a business; (4) Prepare the balance sheet, income statement, statement of retained earnings, and cash flow statement for an economic entity; and (5) Evaluate the financial performance of an economic entity using financial ratios. III. Required Course Material & Important Websites (1) Text – Financial Accounting (Libby, Libby & Hodge, 11e, McGraw-Hill) (2) Basic calculator for exams (cell phones as calculators are not permitted) (3) PowerPoint slides for each chapter (posted on i-Campus) (4) Course website (i-Campus: https://icampus.skku.edu/). IV. Course Format (Flipped Learnings) This course uses a flipped learning format. Each Wednesday, lecture videos are uploaded for each week’s topic. Students are required to watch the uploaded lecture videos online prior to the offline class. Each Tuesday, we will have a face- to-face offline class to discuss what you have learned from the lecture videos and to work on in-class assignments. Please make sure you have access to i -campus. Lecture slides, assignments, or important announcements will be posted on the class website. 2 V. Grading All grading instances are out of 100 points and will be weighted as follows: Attendance & Participation 10 % Assignment 10 % Quiz 10 % Interim Exam 30 % Final Exam 40 % Total 100 % (1) Attendance & Participation (10%) Attendance will be called on offline class days. Circumstances such as medical and family emergencies, job interviews, participation in int er-collegiate athletic contests etc. will not lead to being penalized for attendance score, if properly notifying in advance. publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: Course Description The discipline of accounting and the work of accountants are introduced in two courses, Introduction to Financial Accounting (GBA 2003) and Introduction to Mana gerial Accounting (GBA 2004). Elements of financial accounting are covered in the first course as they relate to the preparation and use of accounting reports for business entities, emphasizing accounting as a provider of financial information for external reporting purposes. Elements of managerial accounting are covered in the second course as they relate to the internal use of accounting information in making business decisions and controlling business operations. II. Learning Outcomes Upon completion of this course you should be able to demonstrate the following; (1) Describe the basic financial statements, their nature, purposes and use by decision makers; (2) Define and/or apply general accounting terms, concepts and processes; (3) Record basic transactions and analyze their impact on the financial statements of a business; (4) Prepare the balance sheet, income statement, statement of retained earnings, and cash flow statement for an economic entity; and (5) Evaluate the financial performance of an economic entity using financial ratios. III. Marketing Management (GBA2006-01)
                          Global Business Administration, SKK Business School
                                                  Fall Semester 2026


GENERAL INFORMATION

Professor:                 Hyejin Lee, Ph.D.

Office:                    Business Building 517


Class schedule:            Monday (13:30-14:45) / Wednesday (12:00-13:15)

Class format***:       PBL (combination of 1. Pre-recorded videos for lectures and 2. Offline classes
                           for students’ activities, discussions, and presentations etc.).

                           *The course calendar below is subject to change to allow flexibility in the
                           course based on the needs of the specific class.

Office hours:              By appointment. The best way to reach me is via i-Campus message.

Recording:                 No recording of any type is permitted without prior instructor approval.

Communication:             Check your i-Campus daily and at least once in the morning before class,
                           since this is the primary way I will contact you regarding course
                           announcements.

                                     Messages, calling, or searching during the class are not permitted.

Required Materials:
    ▪    Course notes for each class will be posted to i-Campus at least 24 hours before class.


Optional Reading:
Please note that this textbook is in no way required for this course. I simply list it as a nice resource
to have for those with a long-term interest in the foundational principles of marketing.
    ▪    Kotler, Philip J. and Gary M. Armstrong (2013), Principles of Marketing (15th Edition).
         Englewood Cliffs, NJ: Prentice Hall.


COURSE DESCRIPTION
                                                                                                                           1

Marketing is everywhere, whether you are purchasing a product online or in a physical store,
watching TV, or reading a magazine at home. Your widespread exposure to marketing can be a
useful learning experience as such exposures provide examples of the marketing concepts we will
discuss this semester. This course is designed to put you in the role of the marketing manager,
someone who delivers marketing to consumers to stimulate purchasing and build loyalty to the
company and its products and services. This course will help you apply marketing concepts and tools
to reach your objectives, such as greater sales, profit, and enhanced consumer welfare. You will also
have the opportunity to relate the course material to your academic major and other areas of personal
interest.

COURSE OUTCOMES

Students enrolled in this course will be able to:
    ▪    Explain the role of marketing in the performance of a team, department, or company.
    ▪    Describe branding and its significance.
    ▪    Identify the target customers or target segment for a product or service using quantitative and
         qualitative data.
    ▪    Set the price of a new product given cost information and data on the price sensitivity of
         target customers.
    ▪    Assess the types of new product introductions that a firm can create and articulate the
         advantages and disadvantages of each.
    ▪    Identify the various promotional strategies and tactics available to a brand and its product
         portfolio and articulate the advantages and disadvantages of each.
    ▪    Summarize, analyze, and articulate marketing solutions in the context of case scenarios.

METHOD OF INSTRUCTION

While the instructional method will lean toward the seminar concept of interaction between the
students and professor, with particular emphasis on the student’s thought process, there will be an
emphasis on individual thought leadership and the role of perspective in differences of opinion.
Students are encouraged to think critically, formulate and defend their position on issues, and
professionally challenge any thoughts, ideas, opinions, and comments made by the professor and
other students.

The course calendar’s topics and assignments should be used as a guide. Student interest in
particular topics and the pace of student learning preclude a precise adherence to the dates outlined
in the topic and assignment sections. Should this occur, I will let you know and we will adjust the
course calendar accordingly.

This course uses i-Campus at SKKU extensively. Course notes, announcements, and other course-
related materials will be posted to i-Campus. It is your responsibility to access course information
and announcements from i-Campus and check i-Campus regularly. If you have connectivity issues,
please contact tech support.



COURSE GRADE DETERMINATION
Course grades will be determined using the following allocation:
                                                                                                                           2

Course Learning Component                                                       %____
Attendance                                                                              10%
Individual/Group Assignments                                                    40%
Midterm and Final Exams                                                         40%
Professionalism                                                                       10%
Total                                                                        100%

1. Attendance:

        - 0 absence (10 points)
        - each absence (10 points - one point from each absence)
        - more than 8 absences (failure in this course); not failure up to 7 absences.
        - late for class 2 times = one absence
        - leaving the classroom early before the class ends = late for class

The only excused absences are: serious illness or the death of an immediate family member

the proper paperwork. Proper documentation for a serious illness requires a doctor’s note indicating
that you are unfit to attend class on that day. A note from the hospital indicating that you were there
is not sufficient documentation. You must get a note indicating you are “unfit” to attend class from
the doctor who assessed you.

2. Individual Assignments/Group Assignments:

1) For individual assignments, you will need to submit several written assignments, with the topic
selected by the instructor. Some of you (or all of you; depending on the class size) will get the
chance to present your assignment on “Individual Assignment Presentation” dates. Details about the
topics will be discussed during the class later.

Turning in Assignments. All assignments must be submitted online to the appropriate folder in i-
Campus before the start of class on the day on which they are due. Assignments received after the
class is scheduled to start will NOT be accepted for credit.

2) For group assignments, a group of 4-5 individuals (depending on the class size) will study one
marketing case and propose effective marketing strategies. Details about this task will be discussed
during the class later. You will need to present your work and your presentation will be evaluated by
your classmates. Your presentation score will be mainly determined based on your peers’
evaluations and my adjustment to them, which I will only do when necessary.

Prevention of Free Riding. Occasionally, some teams experience the so-called “free rider” problem.
If it is brought to my attention that a team is experiencing a free rider problem, that team will be
subject to a within-team peer evaluation whereby each member of the team will evaluate the extent
of the contributions of all the other team members. In this case, the presentation score that is earned
by the team will be lowered for the free riders, who are defined as members whose contributions are
significantly lower than the other team members. However, keep in mind that no teams are good
from the beginning.

                                                                                                                                 3

3. Exams:

1) Each exam consists of questions covering the material in the course notes, readings, and in-class
discussion. The in-class discussion may vary from the PowerPoint decks, so it is essential to take
good notes in class. The exams are not cumulative. The format of the exams will be discussed later
in class.

Makeup Exams. Students with a valid excuse (illness and death of an immediate family member) are
entitled to take a make-up exam. Please note that if you miss the exam due to factors outside of
accepted excuses, you will receive a zero for the exam. The makeup exam format will be different
than the regular exams. The makeup exams are scheduled at the professor’s convenience.

4. Professionalism:

Professional behavior includes, but is not limited to:

1) your participating in class discussions by contributing new and valuable perspectives (especially
in exercises/case discussions),
2) full attention to the classroom discussion (with the camera on),
3) being on time to class (preferably early) and leaving on time (not early),
4) putting all electronic devices away,
5) speaking respectfully to all members of the classroom,
6) being adequately prepared by having read the assigned material for each class,
7) turning all assignments in on time (or early),
8) not disrupting the class by talking to your neighbor(s), and
9) approaching the class with an understanding that your grade is earned and not given (i.e.,
entitled behavior will not be rewarded).

While in-class exercises provide a valuable opportunity to demonstrate professionalism, the
professionalism score encompasses a broader range of behaviors. It reflects your overall attitude,
engagement, and contribution to a respectful and productive learning environment throughout the
course.

10) The easiest way to gain bonus points in professionalism is to participate in in-class exercises;
however, professionalism is evaluated holistically and is not limited to in-class participation alone.

Grade Errors:

If you believe that I assigned an incorrect score on an exam or other class assignment, you must
submit a brief explanation outlining your position within the timeframe that I specify. However,
when I review a specific assignment grade, I reserve the right to adjust the grade in any direction –
either up or down. This includes requests at the end of the semester to reconsider the final grade.
When such a request is made, I reserve the right to take into account the entire semester’s
performance and adjust the grade, up or down, accordingly.

Student Academic Misconduct:



                                                                                                                              4

As the instructor for this course, I am obligated to report all suspected cases of academic misconduct
(e.g., cheating or plagiarism, etc.) to the appropriate university channels. There will be consequences
for academic misconduct including the possibility of failing this course.

COURSE REQUIREMENTS IN DETAIL 1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance Page 3 • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: 1. Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. 2. Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on: (1) peer observation notes collected during randomly selected offline sessions — for each group member, a one-line note on what they did that day (if present) or how actively they've generally participated (if absent); (2) general conduct during offline sessions, at the instructor's discretion; and (3) the Week 2 self-introduction. 3) Semester-long Project: New Product Development (NPD) Project This semester-long project serves as the core practical component of the course, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world application. The ultimate goal is to apply key marketing concepts learned throughout the semester – including strategic analysis, STP, and the 4P mix – to a comprehensive business case. Each group selects a real brand and proposes a product or service in a new category. The extension should make sense to consumers. Groups then investigate the brand, customer needs, the proposed market, and competing products to judge whether the idea is worth developing and refine the proposal. Midway through the semester, each group is randomly assigned a resource-scale tier (S/M/L) and must converge on a final launch plan within that tier – deciding what to keep and what to drop. Up to three groups may select the same brand if their extension categories differ. Detailed instructions and required formats are provided in the separate project guideline. • Marketing Project Plan: A 1–2-page proposal evaluating whether the idea is worth developing. It covers five parts: (1) the selected brand and new product or service idea; (2) brand fit and logical association; (3) customer needs and market outlook; (4) key competitors, competing product comparisons, and differentiation; and (5) the initial target customer and important limitations. Support the proposal with research. A mandatory consultation session with the instructor follows. Page 4 • Group Presentation: The group's final deliverable. Covers the growth gap, the extension logic, STP, and the 4P launch plan within the assigned resource tier. The deck must include two required slides – what the group chose to drop and why, and a consistency check across positioning, offering, and intended consumer impression. Held across two sessions. • Individual Creative Production: An individual assignment extending the group project. Using AI tools now common in marketing practice, each student produces one promotional package (e.g., a short-form video ad, branded content series, virtual brand ambassador, or pop-up experience concept) based on the group's final strategy, along with a one-page brief (Target, Message, Rationale). Detailed options and requirements are provided in a separate guide. Submitting identical or substantially similar work as another group member constitutes academic dishonesty. • Peer Evaluation: At the end of the semester, each student confidentially evaluates their group members' contributions. Individual scores on the group components (Presentation) may be adjusted downward based on peer-evaluation results and the instructor's observation. Free-riding will be reflected in individual grades. 4) Exams There will be two exams, and the dates are listed in the course schedule. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice titled “Request for Thorough University Academic Management,” students who do not take the final exam must receive an F grade for the course. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND POLICIES 1) Course Materials & Copyright All course materials, including online lecture videos, slides, assignments, and exams, are the intellectual property of the instructor and are protected by copyright law. They are intended solely for the personal use of students currently enrolled in the course. • Unauthorized Distribution: Sharing, uploading, or redistributing course materials on any platform without permission is strictly prohibited. • Prohibition of AI Misuse: Using the instructor’s voice, image, or video content to train AI models, create deepfakes, or generate unauthorized synthetic media is a serious violation of personal rights and copyright law. Any such activity will be met with severe legal and disciplinary action. 2) No Recording Policy Page 5 To ensure open discussion and protect the privacy of both the instructor and students, unauthorized audio recording, video filming, or photography during offline sessions is strictly prohibited. • Exceptions are granted only for students with documented disabilities who have received prior approval from the instructor. • Violation of this policy may result in immediate dismissal from the classroom and academic penalties. 3) AI Tool Usage Policy This course follows the university’s AI Education Guidelines (SAFE Framework). AI tools may be used as supplementary aids in the learning process (e.g., brainstorming, idea generation, language polishing); however, all final submissions must reflect the student’s own understanding, judgment, and effort.
