See the table for the specific type assigned to each assignment in this course. • AI Usage Disclosure: If AI tools are used, students must attach a brief AI Usage Statement in the appendix of their submission, indicating which tool was used, for what purpose, and how the output was reviewed or revised by the student. • Grading Impact: Submissions are evaluated on the student’s own critical reasoning and originality. AI-generated content that is undisclosed, unverified, or used beyond the permitted scope will not receive credit for that portion of the work. • Verification & Violations: If no AI Usage Statement is provided, the instructor may verify the work using AI detection software or a short oral follow-up. Undisclosed or out-of-scope use of AI- Page 6 generated content constitutes academic dishonesty under Section 4, and significant penalties will apply, up to a failing grade for the assignment or course. 4) Academic Dishonesty Acts such as cheating, plagiarism, record tampering, unauthorized assistance, or any other conduct violating academic integrity will result in strict disciplinary action. Once dishonesty is confirmed, no appeals or reviews will be permitted. COURSE OBJECTIVES This course introduces core concepts of marketing, focusing on how companies identify and respond to customers' needs and wants through appropriate product and service strategies. It is designed to enhance all students' understanding of marketing activities and provides a framework for analyzing market dynamics. By the end of this semester, students will be able to: 1. Identify and apply essential marketing tools to address marketing challenges. 2. Understand and employ key principles and relevant marketing terminology. 3. Connect marketing knowledge to real-world business situations. COURSE MATERIALS • Required Textbook: MKTG: Principles of Marketing (14th Edition, 2025) by Lamb, Hair and McDaniel, published by Cengage (ISBN: 9789815200720). • Supplementary Materials: Slides and articles will be available on i-Campus. COURSE FORMAT AND POLICIES Under the Flipped Learning model, students must watch the online lecture before class. Offline sessions are dedicated to reinforcing concepts through active participation and the semester-long New Product Development (NPD) project. Students must speak only in English during the offline sessions. Professional behavior is expected. Arrive on time, silence all electronic devices, and avoid personal conversations. Disruptive or unprofessional behavior may result in being asked to leave the classroom with or without prior notice.

Based on your total percentage score, letter grades will be assigned as follows: A+ = 95 - 100%, A = 90 - 94.99%, B+ = 85 - 89.99%, B = 80 - 84.99%, C+ = 75 - 79.99%, C = 70 - 74.99%, D+ = 65 - 69.99%, D = 60 - 64.99%, F = 0 - 59.99%. To ensure fairness and transparency, all appeals must be submitted in writing via a formal document or email. COURSE REQUIREMENTS IN DETAIL 1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance Page 3 • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: 1. Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. 2. Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on: (1) peer observation notes collected during randomly selected offline sessions — for each group member, a one-line note on what they did that day (if present) or how actively they've generally participated (if absent); (2) general conduct during offline sessions, at the instructor's discretion; and (3) the Week 2 self-introduction. 3) Semester-long Project: New Product Development (NPD) Project This semester-long project serves as the core practical component of the course, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world application. The ultimate goal is to apply key marketing concepts learned throughout the semester – including strategic analysis, STP, and the 4P mix – to a comprehensive business case. Each group selects a real brand and proposes a product or service in a new category. The extension should make sense to consumers. Groups then investigate the brand, customer needs, the proposed market, and competing products to judge whether the idea is worth developing and refine the proposal. Midway through the semester, each group is randomly assigned a resource-scale tier (S/M/L) and must converge on a final launch plan within that tier – deciding what to keep and what to drop. Up to three groups may select the same brand if their extension categories differ. Detailed instructions and required formats are provided in the separate project guideline. • Marketing Project Plan: A 1–2-page proposal evaluating whether the idea is worth developing. It covers five parts: (1) the selected brand and new product or service idea; (2) brand fit and logical association; (3) customer needs and market outlook; (4) key competitors, competing product comparisons, and differentiation; and (5) the initial target customer and important limitations. Support the proposal with research. A mandatory consultation session with the instructor follows. Page 4 • Group Presentation: The group's final deliverable. Covers the growth gap, the extension logic, STP, and the 4P launch plan within the assigned resource tier. The deck must include two required slides – what the group chose to drop and why, and a consistency check across positioning, offering, and intended consumer impression. Held across two sessions. • Individual Creative Production: An individual assignment extending the group project. Using AI tools now common in marketing practice, each student produces one promotional package (e.g., a short-form video ad, branded content series, virtual brand ambassador, or pop-up experience concept) based on the group's final strategy, along with a one-page brief (Target, Message, Rationale). Detailed options and requirements are provided in a separate guide. Submitting identical or substantially similar work as another group member constitutes academic dishonesty. • Peer Evaluation: At the end of the semester, each student confidentially evaluates their group members' contributions. Individual scores on the group components (Presentation) may be adjusted downward based on peer-evaluation results and the instructor's observation. Free-riding will be reflected in individual grades. 4) Exams There will be two exams, and the dates are listed in the course schedule. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice titled “Request for Thorough University Academic Management,” students who do not take the final exam must receive an F grade for the course. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND POLICIES 1) Course Materials & Copyright All course materials, including online lecture videos, slides, assignments, and exams, are the intellectual property of the instructor and are protected by copyright law. They are intended solely for the personal use of students currently enrolled in the course. • Unauthorized Distribution: Sharing, uploading, or redistributing course materials on any platform without permission is strictly prohibited. • Prohibition of AI Misuse: Using the instructor’s voice, image, or video content to train AI models, create deepfakes, or generate unauthorized synthetic media is a serious violation of personal rights and copyright law. Any such activity will be met with severe legal and disciplinary action. 2) No Recording Policy Page 5 To ensure open discussion and protect the privacy of both the instructor and students, unauthorized audio recording, video filming, or photography during offline sessions is strictly prohibited. • Exceptions are granted only for students with documented disabilities who have received prior approval from the instructor. • Violation of this policy may result in immediate dismissal from the classroom and academic penalties. 3) AI Tool Usage Policy This course follows the university’s AI Education Guidelines (SAFE Framework). AI tools may be used as supplementary aids in the learning process (e.g., brainstorming, idea generation, language polishing); however, all final submissions must reflect the student’s own understanding, judgment, and effort. University-wide AI usage classification (per AI Education Guidelines, 2026): N-Type D-Type C-Type B-Type A-Type AI use fully prohibited Minimal AI use recommended (idea generation, grammar correction only) Limited AI use permitted (research, drafting) Active AI use permitted AI use/collaboration itself is the object of evaluation AI usage type applied in this course, by assignment: Assignment / Assessment AI Usage Type Marketing Project Plan D – Minimal use recommended (idea generation, grammar correction only) Group Presentation C – Limited use (research, drafting) Individual Creative Production B – Active use permitted (AI verification report required) Midterm / Final Exam N – AI use fully prohibited • Permitted Tools: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and other generative AI tools. • Permitted Scope: Permitted AI usage differs by assignment, following the university-wide N/D/C/B/A classification shown above. See the table for the specific type assigned to each assignment in this course. • AI Usage Disclosure: If AI tools are used, students must attach a brief AI Usage Statement in the appendix of their submission, indicating which tool was used, for what purpose, and how the output was reviewed or revised by the student. • Grading Impact: Submissions are evaluated on the student’s own critical reasoning and originality. AI-generated content that is undisclosed, unverified, or used beyond the permitted scope will not receive credit for that portion of the work. • Verification & Violations: If no AI Usage Statement is provided, the instructor may verify the work using AI detection software or a short oral follow-up. Undisclosed or out-of-scope use of AI- Page 6 generated content constitutes academic dishonesty under Section 4, and significant penalties will apply, up to a failing grade for the assignment or course. 4) Academic Dishonesty Acts such as cheating, plagiarism, record tampering, unauthorized assistance, or any other conduct violating academic integrity will result in strict disciplinary action. Once dishonesty is confirmed, no appeals or reviews will be permitted. The ultimate goal is to apply key marketing concepts learned throughout the semester – including strategic analysis, STP, and the 4P mix – to a comprehensive business case. Each group selects a real brand and proposes a product or service in a new category. The extension should make sense to consumers. Groups then investigate the brand, customer needs, the proposed market, and competing products to judge whether the idea is worth developing and refine the proposal. Midway through the semester, each group is randomly assigned a resource-scale tier (S/M/L) and must converge on a final launch plan within that tier – deciding what to keep and what to drop. Up to three groups may select the same brand if their extension categories differ. Detailed instructions and required formats are provided in the separate project guideline. • Marketing Project Plan: A 1–2-page proposal evaluating whether the idea is worth developing. It covers five parts: (1) the selected brand and new product or service idea; (2) brand fit and logical association; (3) customer needs and market outlook; (4) key competitors, competing product comparisons, and differentiation; and (5) the initial target customer and important limitations. Support the proposal with research. A mandatory consultation session with the instructor follows. Page 4 • Group Presentation: The group's final deliverable. Covers the growth gap, the extension logic, STP, and the 4P launch plan within the assigned resource tier. The deck must include two required slides – what the group chose to drop and why, and a consistency check across positioning, offering, and intended consumer impression. Detailed options and requirements are provided in a separate guide. All scores will be posted on i-Campus before final grades are entered into the university system – review your scores and raise any questions at that stage. Once final grades are submitted, they will not be changed except for clear entry errors. COURSE OBJECTIVES This course introduces core concepts of marketing, focusing on how companies identify and respond to customers' needs and wants through appropriate product and service strategies. It is designed to enhance all students' understanding of marketing activities and provides a framework for analyzing market dynamics. By the end of this semester, students will be able to: 1. Identify and apply essential marketing tools to address marketing challenges. 2. Understand and employ key principles and relevant marketing terminology. 3. Connect marketing knowledge to real-world business situations. COURSE MATERIALS • Required Textbook: MKTG: Principles of Marketing (14th Edition, 2025) by Lamb, Hair and McDaniel, published by Cengage (ISBN: 9789815200720). • Supplementary Materials: Slides and articles will be available on i-Campus. COURSE FORMAT AND POLICIES Under the Flipped Learning model, students must watch the online lecture before class. Offline sessions are dedicated to reinforcing concepts through active participation and the semester-long New Product Development (NPD) project. Students must speak only in English during the offline sessions. Professional behavior is expected. Arrive on time, silence all electronic devices, and avoid personal conversations. Disruptive or unprofessional behavior may result in being asked to leave the classroom with or without prior notice.

1) Attendance (18%) - Online Streaming: 9% - Offline Attendance: 9% 2) Class Participation (5%) 3) Semester-long Project (31%) - Marketing Project Plan: 5% - Group Presentation: 17% - Individual Creative Production: 9% 4) Exams (46%) - Midterm: 23% - Final: 23% Total: 100% Note: All earned points will be converted into a percentage. Based on your total percentage score, letter grades will be assigned as follows: A+ = 95 - 100%, A = 90 - 94.99%, B+ = 85 - 89.99%, B = 80 - 84.99%, C+ = 75 - 79.99%, C = 70 - 74.99%, D+ = 65 - 69.99%, D = 60 - 64.99%, F = 0 - 59.99%. All grades will be posted on i-Campus. In case of any grade entry errors, a correction announcement will be made, and your grade may be adjusted (either upward or downward). Any questions or appeals regarding your scores or final grade must be submitted within two days of the posting. To ensure fairness and transparency, all appeals must be submitted in writing via a formal document or email. COURSE REQUIREMENTS IN DETAIL 1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance Page 2 • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: 1. Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. 2. Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on: (1) peer observation notes collected during randomly selected offline sessions — for each group member, a one-line note on what they did that day (if present) or how actively they've generally participated (if absent); (2) general conduct during offline sessions, at the instructor's discretion; and (3) the Week 2 self-introduction. 3) Semester-long Project: New Product Development (NPD) Project This semester-long project serves as the core practical component of the course, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world application. The ultimate goal is to apply key marketing concepts learned throughout the semester – including strategic analysis, STP, and the 4P mix – to a comprehensive business case. Each group selects a real brand and proposes a product or service in a new category. The extension should make sense to consumers. Groups then investigate the brand, customer needs, the proposed market, and competing products to judge whether the idea is worth developing and refine the proposal. Midway through the semester, each group is randomly assigned a resource-scale tier (S/M/L) and must converge on a final launch plan within that tier – deciding what to keep and what to drop. Up to three groups may select the same brand if their extension categories differ. Detailed instructions and required formats are provided in the separate project guideline. • Marketing Project Plan: A 1–2-page proposal evaluating whether the idea is worth developing. It covers five parts: (1) the selected brand and new product or service idea; (2) brand fit and logical association; (3) customer needs and market outlook; (4) key competitors, competing product comparisons, and differentiation; and (5) the initial target customer and important limitations. Support the proposal with research. A mandatory consultation session with the instructor follows. Page 3 • Group Presentation: The group's final deliverable. Covers the growth gap, the extension logic, STP, and the 4P launch plan within the assigned resource tier. The deck must include two required slides – what the group chose to drop and why, and a consistency check across positioning, offering, and intended consumer impression. Held across two sessions. • Individual Creative Production: An individual assignment extending the group project. Using AI tools now common in marketing practice, each student produces one promotional package (e.g., a short-form video ad, branded content series, virtual brand ambassador, or pop-up experience concept) based on the group's final strategy, along with a one-page brief (Target, Message, Rationale). Detailed options and requirements are provided in a separate guide. Submitting identical or substantially similar work as another group member constitutes academic dishonesty. • Peer Evaluation: At the end of the semester, each student confidentially evaluates their group members' contributions. Individual scores on the group components (Presentation) may be adjusted downward based on peer-evaluation results and the instructor's observation. Free-riding will be reflected in individual grades. 4) Exams There will be two exams, and the dates are listed in the course schedule. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice titled “Request for Thorough University Academic Management,” students who do not take the final exam must receive an F grade for the course. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND POLICIES 1) Course Materials & Copyright All course materials, including online lecture videos, slides, assignments, and exams, are the intellectual property of the instructor and are protected by copyright law. They are intended solely for the personal use of students currently enrolled in the course. • Unauthorized Distribution: Sharing, uploading, or redistributing course materials on any platform without permission is strictly prohibited. • Prohibition of AI Misuse: Using the instructor’s voice, image, or video content to train AI models, create deepfakes, or generate unauthorized synthetic media is a serious violation of personal rights and copyright law. Any such activity will be met with severe legal and disciplinary action. 2) No Recording Policy Page 4 To ensure open discussion and protect the privacy of both the instructor and students, unauthorized audio recording, video filming, or photography during offline sessions is strictly prohibited. • Exceptions are granted only for students with documented disabilities who have received prior approval from the instructor. • Violation of this policy may result in immediate dismissal from the classroom and academic penalties. 3) AI Tool Usage Policy This course follows the university’s AI Education Guidelines (SAFE Framework). AI tools may be used as supplementary aids in the learning process (e.g., brainstorming, idea generation, language polishing); however, all final submissions must reflect the student’s own understanding, judgment, and effort. University-wide AI usage classification (per AI Education Guidelines, 2026): N-Type D-Type C-Type B-Type A-Type AI use fully prohibited Minimal AI use Limited AI use Active AI use AI use/collaboration recommended (idea permitted (research, permitted itself is the object of generation, grammar drafting) evaluation correction only) AI usage type applied in this course, by assignment: Assignment / Assessment AI Usage Type Marketing Project Plan D – Minimal use recommended (idea generation, grammar correction only) Group Presentation C – Limited use (research, drafting) Individual Creative Production B – Active use permitted (AI verification report required) Midterm / Final Exam N – AI use fully prohibited • Permitted Tools: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and other generative AI tools. • Permitted Scope: Permitted AI usage differs by assignment, following the university-wide N/D/C/B/A classification shown above. See the table for the specific type assigned to each assignment in this course. • AI Usage Disclosure: If AI tools are used, students must attach a brief AI Usage Statement in the appendix of their submission, indicating which tool was used, for what purpose, and how the output was reviewed or revised by the student. • Grading Impact: Submissions are evaluated on the student’s own critical reasoning and originality. AI-generated content that is undisclosed, unverified, or used beyond the permitted scope will not receive credit for that portion of the work. • Verification & Violations: If no AI Usage Statement is provided, the instructor may verify the work using AI detection software or a short oral follow-up. Undisclosed or out-of-scope use of AI- Page 5 generated content constitutes academic dishonesty under Section 4, and significant penalties will apply, up to a failing grade for the assignment or course. 4) Academic Dishonesty Acts such as cheating, plagiarism, record tampering, unauthorized assistance, or any other conduct violating academic integrity will result in strict disciplinary action. Once dishonesty is confirmed, no appeals or reviews will be permitted. Week 2 self-introduction. 3) Semester-long Project: New Product Development (NPD) Project This semester-long project serves as the core practical component of the course, designed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and real-world application. The ultimate goal is to apply key marketing concepts learned throughout the semester – including strategic analysis, STP, and the 4P mix – to a comprehensive business case. Each group selects a real brand and proposes a product or service in a new category. The extension should make sense to consumers. Groups then investigate the brand, customer needs, the proposed market, and competing products to judge whether the idea is worth developing and refine the proposal. Midway through the semester, each group is randomly assigned a resource-scale tier (S/M/L) and must converge on a final launch plan within that tier – deciding what to keep and what to drop. Up to three groups may select the same brand if their extension categories differ. Detailed instructions and required formats are provided in the separate project guideline. • Marketing Project Plan: A 1–2-page proposal evaluating whether the idea is worth developing. It covers five parts: (1) the selected brand and new product or service idea; (2) brand fit and logical association; (3) customer needs and market outlook; (4) key competitors, competing product comparisons, and differentiation; and (5) the initial target customer and important limitations. Support the proposal with research. A mandatory consultation session with the instructor follows. Page 3 • Group Presentation: The group's final deliverable. Covers the growth gap, the extension logic, STP, and the 4P launch plan within the assigned resource tier. The deck must include two required slides – what the group chose to drop and why, and a consistency check across positioning, offering, and intended consumer impression. Held across two sessions. • Individual Creative Production: An individual assignment extending the group project. Using AI tools now common in marketing practice, each student produces one promotional package (e.g., a short-form video ad, branded content series, virtual brand ambassador, or pop-up experience concept) based on the group's final strategy, along with a one-page brief (Target, Message, Rationale). Detailed options and requirements are provided in a separate guide. Submitting identical or substantially similar work as another group member constitutes academic dishonesty. • Peer Evaluation: At the end of the semester, each student confidentially evaluates their group members' contributions. Individual scores on the group components (Presentation) may be adjusted downward based on peer-evaluation results and the instructor's observation. Free-riding will be reflected in individual grades. 4) Exams There will be two exams, and the dates are listed in the course schedule. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice titled “Request for Thorough University Academic Management,” students who do not take the final exam must receive an F grade for the course. publishedEducationalOperatingTableSectio: 1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming Page 3 • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: - Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. - Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on three components: general conduct during offline sessions, the Week 2 self-introduction, and weekly team worksheets. A worksheet is distributed for each working session, so teams complete it during the session and submit it at the end of class. Each worksheet is a section of an upcoming project deliverable, so the work carries directly into the graded outputs. 3) Individual Lab Assignment There is one individual lab assignment, based on the lab videos covered after the midterm exam. Each student is assigned an individual version of the dataset, so the numerical answers differ from student to student. Students may discuss the assignment with each other, but each student must run the analysis and write the answers themselves. The use of AI tools is fully prohibited for this assignment (N-type); everything required is covered directly in the lecture and lab videos. Submissions may be verified through AI detection tools, and any violation will be treated as academic dishonesty under Section 4, with penalties up to a failing grade for the course. If you have any doubts, it is your responsibility to ask the instructor for clarification. Late submissions will not be accepted. Page 4 4) Exam There will be a midterm exam on October 26. There will be no final exam. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. 5) Business Project The business project is a semester-long group project. Each team selects one real brand that has been actively marketing over roughly the last two years, diagnoses whether that marketing is reaching consumers as intended, and tests what the brand should change. Teams turn a business situation into a measurable research question, conduct exploratory research with publicly available secondary data to diagnose the problem and generate hypotheses, and then design and run a small pilot survey and analyze it in SPSS to test them. A separate guideline with detailed instructions and required formats will be provided for each deliverable, which are as follows: • Project Plan: The selected brand and the change, what the company said in its own words, and where you will look for data (guideline provided). • Project Milestones: Two graded checkpoints, 4% each: the Descriptive Analysis and the Questionnaire. • Group Presentation: Each team presents in Week 15 (12/7), covering the full arc from the research question through the findings to the recommendation. • Final Report: One report per team, due 12/16 (Wed): introduction and research question, method, findings, diagnosis, recommendations, limitations, and

1) Course Materials & Copyright All course materials, including online lecture videos, slides, assignments, and exams, are the intellectual property of the instructor and are protected by copyright law. They are intended solely for the personal use of students currently enrolled in the course. Page 5 • Unauthorized Distribution: Sharing, uploading, or redistributing course materials on any platform without permission is strictly prohibited. • Prohibition of AI Misuse: Using the instructor’s voice, image, or video content to train AI models, create deepfakes, or generate unauthorized synthetic media is a serious violation of personal rights and copyright law. Any such activity will be met with severe legal and disciplinary action. 2) No Recording Policy To ensure open discussion and protect the privacy of both the instructor and students, unauthorized audio recording, video filming, or photography during offline sessions is strictly prohibited. Exceptions are granted only for students with documented disabilities who have received prior approval from the instructor. Violation of this policy may result in immediate dismissal from the classroom and academic penalties. 3) AI Tool Usage Policy This course follows the university’s AI Education Guidelines (SAFE Framework). AI tools may be used as supplementary aids in the learning process (e.g., brainstorming, idea generation, language polishing); however, all final submissions must reflect the student’s own understanding, judgment, and effort. University-wide AI usage classification (per AI Education Guidelines, 2026): N-Type D-Type C-Type B-Type A-Type AI use fully prohibited Minimal AI use recommended (idea generation, grammar correction only) Limited AI use permitted (research, drafting) Active AI use permitted AI use/collaboration itself is the object of evaluation AI usage type applied in this course, by assignment: Assignment / Assessment AI Usage Type Lab Assignment N – AI use fully prohibited (all required content is covered in the lecture and lab videos) Project Plan (project) D – Minimal use (idea generation, grammar correction only) Descriptive Analysis (project) B – Active use permitted (data-collection code, coding of text data; the team must verify every AI output against the original sources) Questionnaire (project) B – Active use permitted (drafting items and AI-simulated pretests allowed; disclose and verify) Group Presentation C – Limited use (research, drafting) Final Report (team) C – Limited use (research, drafting; writing and interpretation must be the team's own) Midterm Exam N – AI use fully prohibited • Permitted Tools: ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and other generative AI tools. Page 6 • Permitted Scope: Permitted AI usage differs by assignment, following the university-wide N/D/C/B/A classification shown above. See the table for the specific type assigned to each assignment in this course. • AI Usage Disclosure: If AI tools are used, students must attach a brief AI Usage Statement in the appendix of their submission, indicating which tool was used, for what purpose, and how the output was reviewed or revised by the student. • Grading Impact: Submissions are evaluated on the student’s own critical reasoning and originality. AI-generated content that is undisclosed, unverified, or used beyond the permitted scope will not receive credit for that portion of the work. • Verification & Violations: If no AI Usage Statement is provided, the instructor may verify the work using AI detection software or a short oral follow-up. Undisclosed or out-of-scope use of AI-generated content constitutes academic dishonesty under Section 4, and significant penalties will apply, up to a failing grade for the assignment or course. 4) Academic Dishonesty Acts such as cheating, plagiarism, record tampering, unauthorized assistance, or any other conduct violating academic integrity will result in strict disciplinary action. Once dishonesty is confirmed, no appeals or reviews will be permitted. COURSE OBJECTIVES This course is designed to provide an overview of the marketing research process and how it can be used to help businesses make effective marketing decisions. Students will learn how marketing research is carried out through study and practice, including problem definition, research design, data collection, data analysis, and reporting. Students will also work in groups to conduct a marketing research project for a company or brand of their choice. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: - Identify management decision problems and marketing research problems; - Design a questionnaire and implement a survey; - Analyze marketing data using SPSS; - Interpret research findings and make marketing recommendations. COURSE MATERIALS Lecture notes and other class materials will be uploaded to i-Campus (https://icampus.skku.edu/). REQUIRED SOFTWARE SPSS is required software for this course. After the midterm exam, students will learn how to use SPSS and apply it to analyze data related to their business project. To prepare for this, students will need to apply for SPSS access in advance. Further details about the application process will be announced later. COURSE FORMAT AND POLICIES This course follows a flipped learning format (1.5 hours online + 1.5 hours offline). All conceptual content, including the SPSS lab videos, is delivered through the weekly online lectures. Offline sessions are working Page 2 sessions for the semester-long business project: teams work on the current stage of the project and the instructor circulates to give feedback on each team’s progress. At the end of each working session teams submit a one-page worksheet for that week; these count toward Class Participation. • Language Policy: Students must speak only in English during offline sessions. • Conduct: Professional behavior is expected at all times. Arrive on time, use devices for class work only, and avoid personal conversations. Disruptive or unprofessional behavior may result in being asked to leave the classroom, with or without prior notice.

1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming Page 3 • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: - Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. - Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on three components: general conduct during offline sessions, the Week 2 self-introduction, and weekly team worksheets. A worksheet is distributed for each working session, so teams complete it during the session and submit it at the end of class. Each worksheet is a section of an upcoming project deliverable, so the work carries directly into the graded outputs. 3) Individual Lab Assignment There is one individual lab assignment, based on the lab videos covered after the midterm exam. Each student is assigned an individual version of the dataset, so the numerical answers differ from student to student. Students may discuss the assignment with each other, but each student must run the analysis and write the answers themselves. The use of AI tools is fully prohibited for this assignment (N-type); everything required is covered directly in the lecture and lab videos. Submissions may be verified through AI detection tools, and any violation will be treated as academic dishonesty under Section 4, with penalties up to a failing grade for the course. If you have any doubts, it is your responsibility to ask the instructor for clarification. Late submissions will not be accepted. Page 4 4) Exam There will be a midterm exam on October 26. There will be no final exam. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. 5) Business Project The business project is a semester-long group project. Each team selects one real brand that has been actively marketing over roughly the last two years, diagnoses whether that marketing is reaching consumers as intended, and tests what the brand should change. Teams turn a business situation into a measurable research question, conduct exploratory research with publicly available secondary data to diagnose the problem and generate hypotheses, and then design and run a small pilot survey and analyze it in SPSS to test them. A separate guideline with detailed instructions and required formats will be provided for each deliverable, which are as follows: • Project Plan: The selected brand and the change, what the company said in its own words, and where you will look for data (guideline provided). • Project Milestones: Two graded checkpoints, 4% each: the Descriptive Analysis and the Questionnaire. • Group Presentation: Each team presents in Week 15 (12/7), covering the full arc from the research question through the findings to the recommendation. • Final Report: One report per team, due 12/16 (Wed): introduction and research question, method, findings, diagnosis, recommendations, limitations, and

Once final grades are submitted, they will not be changed except for clear entry errors. COURSE OBJECTIVES This course is designed to provide an overview of the marketing research process and how it can be used to help businesses make effective marketing decisions. Students will learn how marketing research is carried out through study and practice, including problem definition, research design, data collection, data analysis, and reporting. Students will also work in groups to conduct a marketing research project for a company or brand of their choice. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: - Identify management decision problems and marketing research problems; - Design a questionnaire and implement a survey; - Analyze marketing data using SPSS; - Interpret research findings and make marketing recommendations. COURSE MATERIALS Lecture notes and other class materials will be uploaded to i-Campus (https://icampus.skku.edu/). REQUIRED SOFTWARE SPSS is required software for this course. After the midterm exam, students will learn how to use SPSS and apply it to analyze data related to their business project. To prepare for this, students will need to apply for SPSS access in advance. Further details about the application process will be announced later. COURSE FORMAT AND POLICIES This course follows a flipped learning format (1.5 hours online + 1.5 hours offline). All conceptual content, including the SPSS lab videos, is delivered through the weekly online lectures. Offline sessions are working Page 1 sessions for the semester-long business project: teams work on the current stage of the project and the instructor circulates to give feedback on each team’s progress. At the end of each working session teams submit a one-page worksheet for that week; these count toward Class Participation. • Language Policy: Students must speak only in English during offline sessions. • Conduct: Professional behavior is expected at all times. Arrive on time, use devices for class work only, and avoid personal conversations. Disruptive or unprofessional behavior may result in being asked to leave the classroom, with or without prior notice.

1) Attendance Attendance consists of two parts: online streaming and offline attendance. According to the Ministry of Education's official notice, students must attend at least three-fourths of the total class hours in order to receive a grade. Accumulating more than 7 absences (online and offline combined) will result in an automatic F grade. Online Streaming Page 2 • The attendance period for lecture videos will be limited to Wednesday through Sunday of each respective week (except for the first week of the semester). • Students must complete the lecture video for that week by Sunday at 11:59pm to receive online attendance credit. • Watching the video after the designated learning period will not be counted. Offline Attendance • Students must check in within 15 minutes after class begins, either through the SKKU Attendance app or by tapping their mobile device or student ID card on the terminal in the classroom. Please be punctual for all sessions. • No penalty to your attendance grade: If you must miss class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance and upload valid documentation, such as a doctor’s note, through the SAM system (https://attend.skku.edu). Absences will be excused only under exceptional conditions and with the instructor's approval. Without proper documentation, the absence will be marked as unexcused. • Penalty on your attendance grade: - Arriving more than 20 minutes late or leaving early. - Missing a class without valid documentation. • Note: Students are responsible for regularly checking their own attendance records. If you believe there is an error or if you missed the check-in on the day of class, you must inform the instructor on the same day. Without a valid excuse and proper documentation, no retroactive changes to attendance records will be allowed. Requests to correct attendance for either online or offline sessions after the final exam and grade posting will not be accepted under any circumstances. 2) Class Participation Class participation is based on three components: general conduct during offline sessions, the Week 2 self- introduction, and weekly team worksheets. A worksheet is distributed for each working session, so teams complete it during the session and submit it at the end of class. Each worksheet is a section of an upcoming project deliverable, so the work carries directly into the graded outputs. 3) Individual Lab Assignment There is one individual lab assignment, based on the lab videos covered after the midterm exam. Each student is assigned an individual version of the dataset, so the numerical answers differ from student to student. Students may discuss the assignment with each other, but each student must run the analysis and write the answers themselves. The use of AI tools is fully prohibited for this assignment (N-type); everything required is covered directly in the lecture and lab videos. Submissions may be verified through AI detection tools, and any violation will be treated as academic dishonesty under Section 4, with penalties up to a failing grade for the course. If you have any doubts, it is your responsibility to ask the instructor for clarification. Late submissions will not be accepted. Page 3 4) Exam There will be a midterm exam on October 26. There will be no final exam. • Policy: Exams must be taken independently. Cheating, sharing, emailing, posting, or collaborating during exams is strictly prohibited. Engaging in any such activities will result in an F for the course, or potentially more severe academic penalties. • Make-up Exams: Exams must be taken in person and on time. Exceptions will be granted only with documented proof of a valid reason, such as a medical emergency, a death in the immediate family, or a scheduled university event. Documentation must be submitted at least three days prior to the exam date. If approved, the instructor may provide a comprehensive make-up exam. • Unexcused Absences: Unexcused absences from exams will result in a failing grade for that exam. 5) Business Project The business project is a semester-long group project. Each team selects one real brand that has been actively marketing over roughly the last two years, diagnoses whether that marketing is reaching consumers as intended, and tests what the brand should change. Teams turn a business situation into a measurable research question, conduct exploratory research with publicly available secondary data to diagnose the problem and generate hypotheses, and then design and run a small pilot survey and analyze it in SPSS to test them. A separate guideline with detailed instructions and required formats will be provided for each deliverable, which are as follows: • Project Plan: The selected brand and the change, what the company said in its own words, and where you will look for data (guideline provided). • Project Milestones: Two graded checkpoints, 4% each: the Descriptive Analysis and the Questionnaire. • Group Presentation: Each team presents in Week 15 (12/7), covering the full arc from the research question through the findings to the recommendation. • Final Report: One report per team, due 12/16 (Wed): introduction and research question, method, findings, diagnosis, recommendations, limitations, and

Sungkyunkwan University                                                                              Dr. Yuna Cho
 SKK Business School                                                                                       Fall 2026

                             GBA2028 ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR

                                       Last updated: August 28, 2026

Contact Information

  Instructor:                          Dr. Yuna Cho
  Office:                              Business School Hall 33208
  Office Hours:                        By appointment

Class Meeting Times  and Locations

Section 01: Monday 9:00am-10:15am & Wednesday 10:30am-11:45am, Classroom 9B218
Section 02: Monday 12:00pm-1:15pm & Wednesday 1:30pm-2:45pm, Classroom 9B218
Section 03: Monday 1:30pm-2:45pm & Wednesday 12:00pm-1:15pm, Classroom 9B218

* This course follows a project-based learning (PBL) format. Each week’s sessions will
combine online lecture videos (usually for Mondays’ sessions) with in-class activities
(usually for Wednesdays’ sessions). You will be asked to watch the videos mostly before,
but sometimes after, coming to class. The weekly schedule is available at the end of this
document.

Course Overview and Objectives

Although skills in finance, accounting, marketing, operations, and strategy are crucial for
achieving success at work, the ability to manage an organization, its groups, and its individuals is
equally important. In your career, you will depend on people to accomplish tasks, goals, and
projects; you will need to work for other people, work with other people, and supervise other
people. Understanding the human side of management is an essential complement to the
technical skills you are learning in other courses.

This course introduces key concepts and topics in organizational behavior (OB), focusing on
individual, interpersonal, and organizational levels. We will cover topics such as decision-making,
motivation, groups and teams, leadership, and organizational structure and culture.

This course takes an integrative and experiential approach, drawing from social science
foundations. Our orientation will be both analytical and managerial, focusing on the
development of concepts and strategies that general managers can use to enhance the value of
the people in their organizations. To integrate the conceptual and applied material, we will use a
series of cases and in-class activities illustrating both successes and failures. Each case and/or
activity will provide an opportunity to use the conceptual material in an analytic way.

Because managing people is inherently experiential, your personal insights are an important part
of the learning process. Your previous experiences, both positive and negative, are an invaluable
source of data for this learning.

The course is designed to accomplish three main goals:
    •    Increase your knowledge of OB concepts so that you can understand and analyze how
         organizations and the people within them work.
    •    Provide you with opportunities to apply OB concepts to real-world problems faced by
         managers.


                                                          1

    •    Develop your leadership and management potential. Effective leaders often manage
         people and information to accomplish organizational goals under conditions not entirely
         in their control. Leaders must successfully be able to diagnose problems, communicate
         clearly, make effective decisions, motivate and influence others, manage diversity, and
         drive organizational change.

Course Requirements

         A-1.      Attendance:                                                                   10 points
         A-2.      Participation:                                                                20 points
         B.        Team Project:                                                                 35 points
         C.        Final Exam:                                                                   35 points
                   Total                                                                         100 points

    A.   Attendance and Participation (30 points)

         A-1. Attendance (10 points): Your attendance per session will be recorded during the entire
         semester. Two unexcused absences will result in an automatic penalty of 5% of the total
         points available in the course. Three or more unexcused absences will result in an automatic
         penalty of 10% of the total points available in the course. In addition, SKKU policies
         indicate that students who fail to achieve 75 percent of attendance (i.e., more than four
         absences) should get an F as a final grade.

         A-2. Participation (20 points): I believe that the best way to learn, especially about OB, is
         to actively participate in your education. In this class, “participation” is defined in terms of
         enriching the learning of your classmates by contributing thoughtfully to class discussion
         and exercises.

         Each week, you will be asked to complete a Discussion Contribution Report based on a
         self-assessment of your participation that week. The reports will be in a short survey form
         and due by end of day (11:59pm) every Sunday. Discussion Contribution scores will be
         summed at the end of the semester.

         The Discussion Contribution Report will ask you to rate yourself each week using a                          1-3
         scale. “1” means no contribution to the discussion, “2” indicates a minimal contribution
         to the discussion, and “3” represents a significant contribution to the discussion (see the
         Discussion Contribution Report for more details).

         For example, if student A rated himself/herself “1” for three weeks, “2” for four weeks,
         “3” for three weeks (total of ten reports submitted), student A would receive a final score
         of 20 participation points:
                                      (1*3=3) + (2*4=8) + (3*3=9) = 20 points

         This  system  to  keep       track  of  discussion  contribution  requires  your  honesty  and  is
         essentially an honor system. I will be reviewing your self-ratings and reserve the right to
         make changes (upward or downward) to your ratings.

         Here are my expectations for your participation:

                   Enrich the conversation. There at least five ways to participate effectively: (1) ask
         a thought-provoking question, (2) share an example of a course concept from your

                                                            2

         experience, (3) stimulate debate by respectfully challenging a point made, (4) build on a
         prior comment to deepen understanding, and (5) integrate course readings insightfully.

                   Be  brave.     Everyone  in  this  class  is  smart,  interesting,  and  has  unique  life
         experiences to share. You will get the most out of this course if you ask questions, voice
         opinions, and express your thoughts to one another.

                   Be engaged.        To make the learning environment as engaging as possible for
         class, except for note-taking purposes. Please refrain from multitasking. The misuse of an
         electronic  device  (e.g.,  surfing  the  web  or  texting)            can   adversely  affect  your  class
         participation grade.

         The quality of the course heavily depends on your attendance and participation. Please be
         reminded that your contribution will be essential not only for your final grade but also for
         the overall class atmosphere and your classmates’ motivation for learning.

    B.   Team Project (35 points)

         At the beginning of the semester (by the end of Week 4), you will form a team of 5~6
         students (exact number to be determined after class size is finalized); you will stay in the
         same team for the whole semester. With your team, you will engage in                          a “consulting”
         project. Each team will conduct an analysis involving the examination of an OB-related
         challenge or issue of concern in a real organization. You may start either by identifying a
         challenge of interest (e.g., what can employers do to retain high-performing employees
         who want a better work-life balance?) and analyzing how the challenge is handled in an
         organization, or you can start by selecting an organization of interest and then identifying
         a salient behavioral challenge that organization is facing.

         You can choose a public, private, or not-for-profit organization (or part of one) to study.
         You should focus your analysis by applying the concepts from the course. Please aim for
         depth rather than breadth regarding the use of course concepts (e.g., do not present a
         review of multiple organizational issues involving multiple concepts taught in this course).
         You will have to contact the organization directly, so it is helpful if one of your team
         members knows someone who works at or is affiliated with the organization you are
         studying (i.e., a friend or relative). You will gather information by looking at any company
         materials (website, brochures, etc.) and by interviewing at least two members of the organization
         parts of the organization or work group. You will also use scholarly sources to research
         the topic beyond what we have covered in class.

         Further guidance and details about the specific grading rubrics will be provided during the
         semester, but the required deliverables for the Team Consulting Project are as follows:

         B-1. Proposal (10 points): The first objective of this proposal is to identify and contact the
         main organization/unit that your team is commonly interested in and wants to conduct
         research on. The second           objective    is for your team to embark on field research by
         conducting at least one interview and implementing an initial analysis of the interview. In
         your proposal report, your team will briefly describe the organization you will study and
         any relevant details (size, industry, location, and others) as well as the OB challenge/issue
         you are interested in studying. This report will be submitted during the midterm week.

                                                            3

         B-2. Presentation (25 points): Your team will deliver a 10-15 minute presentation to the
         class during the final weeks of the semester. The presentation should focus on the OB
         challenge and offer the highlights of your team’s analysis and recommendations.

         For the team-based assignment, everybody in your team should typically receive the same
         score. However, your score might be subject to an individual adjustment at the end of the
         semester, which aims to identify uneven contributions and reallocate the scores within your
         team. To that end, you will be invited to take an online survey after the Team Project to
         let me know about your experience with the team.                     This   survey will be kept strictly
         confidential, and I will NOT discuss your responses with your teammates or any other
         parties without your approval. I may follow up with you if I would like to know further
         details about your responses. Failure to complete the survey will result in a 5 point off in
         your individual grade.

         Bear in mind, though, that the best teamwork should expect no individual adjustment.

    C.   Final Exam (35 points)

         There will be one in-person, closed-book exam at the end of the semester. The exam will
         evaluate your understanding of the class materials and how to apply them. Exam content
         will be drawn from various outlets such as, but not limited to, class slides, other assigned
         readings, cases, and in-class discussion. The exam will be in a multiple-choice format.

         More details regarding the exam and its structure will be provided during the semester.































                                                           4

Sungkyunkwan University                                                                              Dr. Yuna Cho
 SKK Business School                                                                                       Fall 2026

                             GBA2028 ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOR

                                       Last updated: August 28, 2026

Contact Information

  Instructor:                          Dr. Yuna Cho
  Office:                              Business School Hall 33208
  Office Hours:                        By appointment

Class Meeting Times  and Locations

Section 01: Monday 9:00am-10:15am & Wednesday 10:30am-11:45am, Classroom 9B218
Section 02: Monday 12:00pm-1:15pm & Wednesday 1:30pm-2:45pm, Classroom 9B218
Section 03: Monday 1:30pm-2:45pm & Wednesday 12:00pm-1:15pm, Classroom 9B218

* This course follows a project-based learning (PBL) format. Each week’s sessions will
combine online lecture videos (usually for Mondays’ sessions) with in-class activities
(usually for Wednesdays’ sessions). You will be asked to watch the videos mostly before,
but sometimes after, coming to class. The weekly schedule is available at the end of this
document.

Course Overview and Objectives

Although skills in finance, accounting, marketing, operations, and strategy are crucial for
achieving success at work, the ability to manage an organization, its groups, and its individuals is
equally important. In your career, you will depend on people to accomplish tasks, goals, and
projects; you will need to work for other people, work with other people, and supervise other
people. Understanding the human side of management is an essential complement to the
technical skills you are learning in other courses.

This course introduces key concepts and topics in organizational behavior (OB), focusing on
individual, interpersonal, and organizational levels. We will cover topics such as decision-making,
motivation, groups and teams, leadership, and organizational structure and culture.

This course takes an integrative and experiential approach, drawing from social science
foundations. Our orientation will be both analytical and managerial, focusing on the
development of concepts and strategies that general managers can use to enhance the value of
the people in their organizations. To integrate the conceptual and applied material, we will use a
series of cases and in-class activities illustrating both successes and failures. Each case and/or
activity will provide an opportunity to use the conceptual material in an analytic way.

Because managing people is inherently experiential, your personal insights are an important part
of the learning process. Your previous experiences, both positive and negative, are an invaluable
source of data for this learning.

The course is designed to accomplish three main goals:
    •    Increase your knowledge of OB concepts so that you can understand and analyze how
         organizations and the people within them work.
    •    Provide you with opportunities to apply OB concepts to real-world problems faced by
         managers.


                                                          1

    •    Develop your leadership and management potential. Effective leaders often manage
         people and information to accomplish organizational goals under conditions not entirely
         in their control. Leaders must successfully be able to diagnose problems, communicate
         clearly, make effective decisions, motivate and influence others, manage diversity, and
         drive organizational change.

Course Requirements

         A-1.      Attendance:                                                                   10 points
         A-2.      Participation:                                                                20 points
         B.        Team Project:                                                                 35 points
         C.        Final Exam:                                                                   35 points
                   Total                                                                         100 points

    A.   Attendance and Participation (30 points)

         A-1. Attendance (10 points): Your attendance per session will be recorded during the entire
         semester. Two unexcused absences will result in an automatic penalty of 5% of the total
         points available in the course. Three or more unexcused absences will result in an automatic
         penalty of 10% of the total points available in the course. In addition, SKKU policies
         indicate that students who fail to achieve 75 percent of attendance (i.e., more than four
         absences) should get an F as a final grade.

         A-2. Participation (20 points): I believe that the best way to learn, especially about OB, is
         to actively participate in your education. In this class, “participation” is defined in terms of
         enriching the learning of your classmates by contributing thoughtfully to class discussion
         and exercises.

         Each week, you will be asked to complete a Discussion Contribution Report based on a
         self-assessment of your participation that week. The reports will be in a short survey form
         and due by end of day (11:59pm) every Sunday. Discussion Contribution scores will be
         summed at the end of the semester.

         The Discussion Contribution Report will ask you to rate yourself each week using a                          1-3
         scale. “1” means no contribution to the discussion, “2” indicates a minimal contribution
         to the discussion, and “3” represents a significant contribution to the discussion (see the
         Discussion Contribution Report for more details).

         For example, if student A rated himself/herself “1” for three weeks, “2” for four weeks,
         “3” for three weeks (total of ten reports submitted), student A would receive a final score
         of 20 participation points:
                                      (1*3=3) + (2*4=8) + (3*3=9) = 20 points

         This  system  to  keep       track  of  discussion  contribution  requires  your  honesty  and  is
         essentially an honor system. I will be reviewing your self-ratings and reserve the right to
         make changes (upward or downward) to your ratings.

         Here are my expectations for your participation:

                   Enrich the conversation. There at least five ways to participate effectively: (1) ask
         a thought-provoking question, (2) share an example of a course concept from your

                                                            2

         experience, (3) stimulate debate by respectfully challenging a point made, (4) build on a
         prior comment to deepen understanding, and (5) integrate course readings insightfully.

                   Be  brave.     Everyone  in  this  class  is  smart,  interesting,  and  has  unique  life
         experiences to share. You will get the most out of this course if you ask questions, voice
         opinions, and express your thoughts to one another.

                   Be engaged.        To make the learning environment as engaging as possible for
         class, except for note-taking purposes. Please refrain from multitasking. The misuse of an
         electronic  device  (e.g.,  surfing  the  web  or  texting)            can   adversely  affect  your  class
         participation grade.

         The quality of the course heavily depends on your attendance and participation. Please be
         reminded that your contribution will be essential not only for your final grade but also for
         the overall class atmosphere and your classmates’ motivation for learning.

    B.   Team Project (35 points)

         At the beginning of the semester (by the end of Week 4), you will form a team of 5~6
         students (exact number to be determined after class size is finalized); you will stay in the
         same team for the whole semester. With your team, you will engage in                          a “consulting”
         project. Each team will conduct an analysis involving the examination of an OB-related
         challenge or issue of concern in a real organization. You may start either by identifying a
         challenge of interest (e.g., what can employers do to retain high-performing employees
         who want a better work-life balance?) and analyzing how the challenge is handled in an
         organization, or you can start by selecting an organization of interest and then identifying
         a salient behavioral challenge that organization is facing.

         You can choose a public, private, or not-for-profit organization (or part of one) to study.
         You should focus your analysis by applying the concepts from the course. Please aim for
         depth rather than breadth regarding the use of course concepts (e.g., do not present a
         review of multiple organizational issues involving multiple concepts taught in this course).
         You will have to contact the organization directly, so it is helpful if one of your team
         members knows someone who works at or is affiliated with the organization you are
         studying (i.e., a friend or relative). You will gather information by looking at any company
         materials (website, brochures, etc.) and by interviewing at least two members of the organization
         parts of the organization or work group. You will also use scholarly sources to research
         the topic beyond what we have covered in class.

         Further guidance and details about the specific grading rubrics will be provided during the
         semester, but the required deliverables for the Team Consulting Project are as follows:

         B-1. Proposal (10 points): The first objective of this proposal is to identify and contact the
         main organization/unit that your team is commonly interested in and wants to conduct
         research on. The second           objective    is for your team to embark on field research by
         conducting at least one interview and implementing an initial analysis of the interview. In
         your proposal report, your team will briefly describe the organization you will study and
         any relevant details (size, industry, location, and others) as well as the OB challenge/issue
         you are interested in studying. This report will be submitted during the midterm week.

                                                            3

         B-2. Presentation (25 points): Your team will deliver a 10-15 minute presentation to the
         class during the final weeks of the semester. The presentation should focus on the OB
         challenge and offer the highlights of your team’s analysis and recommendations.

         For the team-based assignment, everybody in your team should typically receive the same
         score. However, your score might be subject to an individual adjustment at the end of the
         semester, which aims to identify uneven contributions and reallocate the scores within your
         team. To that end, you will be invited to take an online survey after the Team Project to
         let me know about your experience with the team.                     This   survey will be kept strictly
         confidential, and I will NOT discuss your responses with your teammates or any other
         parties without your approval. I may follow up with you if I would like to know further
         details about your responses. Failure to complete the survey will result in a 5 point off in
         your individual grade.

         Bear in mind, though, that the best teamwork should expect no individual adjustment.

    C.   Final Exam (35 points)

         There will be one in-person, closed-book exam at the end of the semester. The exam will
         evaluate your understanding of the class materials and how to apply them. Exam content
         will be drawn from various outlets such as, but not limited to, class slides, other assigned
         readings, cases, and in-class discussion. The exam will be in a multiple-choice format.

         More details regarding the exam and its structure will be provided during the semester.
