[Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. 1) Global market / Globalization [Orientation] Give a brief overview of the syllabus. Ask any questions you may have by email or iCampus message. As the list of students will be finalized by the second week, class discussion groups will be announced then on iCampus. [Introduction] Introduce the concept of the global market, which will be studied during the semester, and examine why it is important to learn about and explore it. By providing a basic introduction, students will be able to answer the following questions after the first week of class: - What is the global market? - How has globalization affected global consumer culture in recent times? - Why do we need to keep an eye on the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? [Reading] OECD, (2024.10.25.). Students will learn about consumer experiences and trends in social commerce, omni-channel and artificial intelligence, and apply them to real-world examples through discussion. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How has digital technology affected global consumer trends? - What are the consumer trends in global markets driven by digital experiences? Week 10 - Foundation of the global marketplace (2) Global retail chains / Climate crisis [Main Contents & Questions] The retail structure of the global market is the focus this week. Students will learn about how the world is now organized as a marketplace, the interconnected structures that distribute goods to consumers, and apply the theory by looking at real world examples. Through discussion, students will share their own real-life consumer behaviors to shed light on the supply chain behind these purchases. In addition, the viewing material (documentary) will provide an opportunity to critically examine the environmental and socio-economic implications of the current global market structure and consider ways in which it could be improved. This will lead to a critique of the problems with global markets that will be discussed over the next few weeks. By the end of this week, students should be able to answer the following question: - How is the distribution structure of the global market organized? - What are the problems with the current distribution structure of the global market? Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? Ask any questions you may have by email or iCampus message. As the list of students will be finalized by the second week, class discussion groups will be announced then on iCampus. [Introduction] Introduce the concept of the global market, which will be studied during the semester, and examine why it is important to learn about and explore it. By providing a basic introduction, students will be able to answer the following questions after the first week of class: - What is the global market? - How has globalization affected global consumer culture in recent times? - Why do we need to keep an eye on the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? [Reading] OECD, (2024.10.25.). How Shein Built a $66B Fast-Fashion Empire | WSJ The Economics Of, Available at: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gWotBPtsulo&t=406s Week 9 - Foundation of the global marketplace (1) Digital transformation / Digital consumer trends [Main Contents & Questions] Explore the digital landscape and the consumer trends within it that have made global markets more interconnected than ever before. Students will learn about consumer experiences and trends in social commerce, omni-channel and artificial intelligence, and apply them to real-world examples through discussion. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How has digital technology affected global consumer trends? - What are the consumer trends in global markets driven by digital experiences? The Impact Of Digital Transformation On Retail Management And Consumer Behavior. IOSR Journal of Business and Management (IOSR-JBM) e-ISSN, 06-14. Week 10 - Foundation of the global marketplace (2) Global retail chains / Climate crisis [Main Contents & Questions] The retail structure of the global market is the focus this week. Students will learn about how the world is now organized as a marketplace, the interconnected structures that distribute goods to consumers, and apply the theory by looking at real world examples. Through discussion, students will share their own real-life consumer behaviors to shed light on the supply chain behind these purchases. In addition, the viewing material (documentary) will provide an opportunity to critically examine the environmental and socio-economic implications of the current global market structure and consider ways in which it could be improved. This will lead to a critique of the problems with global markets that will be discussed over the next few weeks. By the end of this week, students should be able to answer the following question: - How is the distribution structure of the global market organized? - What are the problems with the current distribution structure of the global market? Students will learn about globalization and localization by examining and comparing examples of companies in today’s global marketplace. Students will also develop a critical awareness by learning about acculturation and cultural homogenization and why they can be problematic. Students will broaden their horizons by researching and sharing real-life examples of acculturation and cultural homogenization issues in the global marketplace. After this week’s lectures, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What are globalization/localization/acculturation/cultural homogenization and how do they differ? - Why can acculturation and cultural homogenization be problematic in the global marketplace? Students are encouraged to think critically about the economics of global markets by examining the underlying problems of unbalanced global market structures and the economic problems experienced at the consumer level as a result of global inflation. Through discussion, students will explore real world examples to deepen their understanding of economic issues in the global marketplace. After this week’s lectures, students will be able to answer the following questions: - How are economic imbalances in global markets structured and how have they evolved historically? - How is global inflation a problem at the consumer level? [Introduction] Introduce the concept of the global market, which will be studied during the semester, and examine why it is important to learn about and explore it. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? 1) Global market / Globalization [Orientation] Give a brief overview of the syllabus. Ask any questions you may have by email or iCampus message. As the list of students will be finalized by the second week, class discussion groups will be announced then on iCampus. [Introduction] Introduce the concept of the global market, which will be studied during the semester, and examine why it is important to learn about and explore it. By providing a basic introduction, students will be able to answer the following questions after the first week of class: - What is the global market? - How has globalization affected global consumer culture in recent times? - Why do we need to keep an eye on the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 2 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (2) Global consumer culture / Universalism / Cross-cultural consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about universalism in the global marketplace, while looking at cross-cultural consumer behavior. We will examine the universal characteristics of consumer markets and explore the implications of ‘universality’ in an unprecedentedly connected global age. Despite the interconnectedness of the world as a single marketplace, different cultures still have their own distinctive characteristics, resulting in differentiated consumer behavior. By the end of this week’s lecture, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What is universalism in the global market? - How does consumer behavior vary by culture? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 1. Consumer Behavior Across Cultures Week 3 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (3) Global consumer culture / Values / Norms / Comparative culture [Main Contents & Questions] Learn what values and norms are and how they exist in the context of culture. Students will learn about some of the most commonly discussed cultural distinctions in the literature and explore how values and norms vary across these distinctions. Students will learn about comparative cultural studies and use it to discuss real-life examples in class. By the end of the week, students should be able to answer the following questions: - What are values and norms and how do they relate to culture? - How does consumer behavior differ across cultures in the global marketplace according to comparative cultural studies? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 2. Values and Cultures Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? Week 4 - Sociocultural aspects of the global market (4) Global consumer culture / Convergence and divergence in consumer behavior [Main Contents & Questions] Learn about the various factors that influence consumer behavior in the global marketplace. Externally influenced by a variety of factors, consumer behavior can converge or diverge in different directions. We will explore the characteristics of these consumer cultures and apply them through discussion of real-world examples. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer the following questions: - What factors influence consumer behavior in the global market? - What are the characteristics of consumer cultures in the global market? [Readings] De Mooij, & Marieke K. (2019). Consumer Behavior and Culture: Consequences for Global Marketing and Advertising, Chapter 3. Convergence and Divergence in Consumer Behavior Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 4. Global Cultural Environment and Buying Behavior Week 5 - Economic aspects of the global market (1) Economic background of global market expansion [Main Contents & Questions] Learn the fundamentals of why the global market is essential in terms of market structure. Students will explore the structural background to economic flows, including domestic market saturation, emerging markets, and the forces of global competition and cooperation. Based on their learning, students will discuss why global markets have become more expansive in the modern era, deepening their understanding of the economic structures of global markets and their impact on consumers. By the end of this weekly lesson, students will be able to answer the following questions: - Why are global markets essential in terms of market structure, and what are the key factors driving their expansion? - In what ways do global competition and cooperation influence consumer behavior and economic flows in globalized markets? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 1. Globalization Imperative Week 6 - Economic aspects of the global market (2) International macroeconomics / International economic indicators / Global market structure [Main Contents & Questions] Take an in-depth look at the economic organization of global consumer markets. Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Students will then study the structure of competition in global markets by examining the distribution of human and technological resources and national competitiveness in global markets at a qualitative level. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? [Reading] Masaaki Kotobe, & Kristiaan Helsen, (2020). Global Marketing Management, Chapter 2. Economic Environment Week 7 - Economic aspects of the global market (3) Developed and Emerging markets [Main Contents & Questions] Examine the economic size and economic relationships of developed and emerging economies in the global consumer marketplace. Compare the differences in economic contexts and how these two classes of countries participate in global markets today. In addition, students will examine real-world examples to understand how global companies shape consumer markets in developed and emerging economies and influence consumer behavior. Through discussion, students will independently investigate real-world cases and apply their learning. By the end of this week, students will be able to answer the following question: - How do developed and emerging economies engage differently in global consumer markets in terms of market structure and consumer impact? [Reading] OECD, (2024.10.25.). By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How has digital technology affected global consumer trends? - What are the consumer trends in global markets driven by digital experiences? Week 10 - Foundation of the global marketplace (2) Global retail chains / Climate crisis [Main Contents & Questions] The retail structure of the global market is the focus this week. Students will learn about how the world is now organized as a marketplace, the interconnected structures that distribute goods to consumers, and apply the theory by looking at real world examples. Through discussion, students will share their own real-life consumer behaviors to shed light on the supply chain behind these purchases. In addition, the viewing material (documentary) will provide an opportunity to critically examine the environmental and socio-economic implications of the current global market structure and consider ways in which it could be improved. This will lead to a critique of the problems with global markets that will be discussed over the next few weeks. By the end of this week, students should be able to answer the following question: - How is the distribution structure of the global market organized? - What are the problems with the current distribution structure of the global market? Students will learn about various international macroeconomic indicators, such as GDP, PPP, and CPI, to understand how these metrics reflect the size and dynamics of global consumer markets. Through discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the qualitative and quantitative economic structure of global consumer markets by discussing the resources and various economic indicators that affect competitiveness in contemporary global marketplace. By the end of the week, students will be able to answer questions such as: - How do GDP, PPP and CPI provide insights into the economic strength of global consumer markets? - What are the key components of the economic structure of global consumer markets, and how do they influence consumer behavior? FinTech and Financial Consumers
                                                     Syllabus


Course Information
         Course Title: FinTech and Financial Consumers
         Academic Year/Semester: Fall 2026
         Course Number-Section: CON3036-01
         Course Type: Major
         Instructor: Prof. HyungJin Ko
         Office: Faculty Hall, Room 40323
         Course Delivery: Project-based learning, PBL (pre-recorded online + in-person)
                Pre-recorded online lectures (weekly)
                In-person (offline) classes (weekly, 1 hour 45 minutes in a regular week)
                In a regular week, the in-person class runs 19:00–20:45, and the remaining time is
                 covered by pre-recorded online lectures.
                On selected days (exams, team project presentations, or sessions with extensive hands-
                 on practice), the entire 18:00–20:45 block is held in person with no online lecture.
                 These dates are announced at least one week in advance.
                The balance between online and in-person hours may be adjusted at the instructor's
                 discretion.
         Semester Period: August 31 – December 18, 2026
         Class Day/Time: Monday, 18:00–20:45
         Classroom: Hoam Hall, Room 50407


Course Objectives
          This course covers financial artificial intelligence and financial AI agents within the field of
           financial technology (fintech), equipping students with practical skills to apply these
           technologies to portfolio management, wealth management, and retirement planning for
           financial consumers. Building on this foundation, the course analyzes the impact of fintech
           on financial consumer behavior and explores its effects on life-cycle asset management and
           retirement financial planning. By the end of this course, students will gain a comprehensive
           and practical understanding of innovations in modern financial technology and their societal
           impact from both technical and consumer studies perspectives.


Course Purpose & Target Students
          This course is designed to develop practical skills for students seeking careers or academic
           pursuits in fintech or financial AI.
          The course is intended for students who wish to gain not only a comprehensive
           understanding of fintech and financial consumers but also practical, in-depth knowledge in
           areas such as retirement management, investment, financial planning, asset management,
           and robo-advisor systems.
          This course is for students who are willing to put forth their best effort and remain fully
           committed throughout the semester.
Prerequisites
          (Required) Completion of 'Introduction to FinTech' and ‘Artificial Intelligence Data Analytics’
           is required.   (These courses may be completed at any time prior to registering for "Fintech
           and Financial Consumers."). Or equivalent.
          (Strongly Recommended) Elementary Probability and Statistics or equivalent
          (Strongly Recommended) Elementary Linear Algebra and Calculus or equivalent
          Students will only be able to keep up with the course material if they have completed
           courses in elementary probability and statistics, linear algebra, and calculus, or have already
           acquired equivalent knowledge, or are willing to diligently preview the materials provided
           in this course.

Contents (Main Topic)
          Financial Consumers and FinTech
                Impact of FinTech on Financial Consumers: Accessibility and Financial Inclusion
                Problems of Financial Consumers: Financial Literacy and the Underserved
          Two Asset Portfolio (Risky Asset + Risk Free Asset)
                N:1-N Portfolio (Asset Allocation)
                      N:1-N B&H
                      N:1-N adjusting (Rebalancing)
          Financial Consumer Profiling and Risk Preference
                Risk Aversion and Risk Tolerance
                Utility and Optimal Portfolio Choice
                Consumer Profile and Risk Tolerance Questionnaire
          Retirement Planning
                Sequence and Longevity Risk
                      Sequence-of-Return Risk
                      Longevity Risk
                2 Stages (Phases) of Asset Management (Financial Planning)
                      1st Phase: Set up for Asset Management (Wealth Accumulation)
                      2nd Phase: Set up for Retirement Management (Wealth Decumulation)
                Strategy for 2nd Phase
                      Static Strategy
                      Dynamic Strategy
          Multi Asset Portfolio
                Rule of Thumb
                Mathematical (Optimization-based) Framework
                      Mean-Variance
                      Black-Litterman
                      Risk Parity
                Factor Investing
          Performance Measures
                Return and Risk Measures
                      Cumulative and Annualized Return
                      Volatility
                      Sharpe Ratio
                      Maximum Drawdown
                      Historical Value at Risk (95%)
                Retirement Portfolio Measures
                      Depletion Probability
                      Maximum Decline
                      Underwater Duration
                      Total Withdrawal
                      Bequest
          Robo-Advisory for Financial Consumers
                Service Architecture and Consumer Benefits
                AI-Powered Robo-Advisor
          Financial Artificial Intelligence
                Model-based Classification
                      Machine Learning-based
                      Deep Learning-based
                      GenAI-based
                      (L)LM-based
                Task-based Classification
                      Estimation Error
                      Bottleneck in Investment Process
                Applications for Financial Consumers (Credit Risk, Fraud Detection, Alternative Data)
                Trustworthy AI: Fairness and Explainable AI (XAI)
          Financial AI Agent
                AI Agent
                Multi-Agent Systems
                Model Context Protocol (MCP)
                Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
          Financial Consumer Protection and Privacy
                Financial Consumer Protection Act and Mis-selling
                Privacy Enhancing Technologies


Reading Materials
          Instead of a specific textbook, the main course materials will consist of lecture notes and
           slides that will be uploaded to the I-campus before each weekly session.


Course Supplies
          Students must bring their laptops for practical exercises
          A Claude Pro (or higher) or ChatGPT Plus (or higher) subscription is required.


Project
          (SCI(E)/SSCI/Conference) Paper writing (practice) (Financial AI-related)
          Portfolio management practice (Accumulation and Decumulation Phase)


Grading Policy
          Grades will be based on exams (final exam 30%), projects (60%), class participation (5%),
           and attendance (5%).
          Grades will be determined by exam performance and overall class participation.
          Students whose exam scores fall within the lowest percentile will receive an "F" grade.
          Exchange and international students will be held to the same standards as Korean students
           —no exceptions or accommodations will be made.
          Policies regarding grading, attendance, and exams will be applied strictly without exception.
          Students who intentionally disclose exam content may face disciplinary consequences.
Important Notices
           Before enrolling, read these guidelines thoroughly. Do not register for this course unless you
            are fully prepared to follow them.
           Do not enroll unless you agree to the rigorous grading standards.
           Maximum dedication and hard work are expected from all enrolled students.
           Students are solely responsible for any missed urgent announcements sent via I-Campus
           An active LLM subscription (at minimum Claude Pro or ChatGPT Plus) must be maintained
            throughout the semester.
           This course is project-intensive and involves discussions and Q&A sessions conducted in
            Korean. As the course is taught in Korean, students must be able to communicate fluently in
            Korean to participate fully. Students who have difficulty communicating in Korean are
            advised to choose a different course. Students with limited Korean proficiency will not
            receive any special consideration.

      행동에 미치는 영향을 분석하고,       생애주기별 자산 관리 및 은퇴 재무 계획에 미치는
      효과를 탐구함.   본 과목을 이수한 학생은 현대 금융 기술의 혁신과 그 사회적
      영향을 기술적 관점과 소비자학적 관점 모두에서 종합적이고 실무적으로 이해할 수
      있게 됨.



수강 목적 및 대상

    본  과목은 핀테크 또는 금융 인공지능 분야 업계나 학계에 진출하고자 하는 학생들의
     실용적 역량을 키우기 위한 수업임.
       본  과목은     핀테크와 금융소비자에 대한 포괄적인 개념 이해 뿐만 아니라,  은퇴관리,
        투자,  재무설계,     자산관리,     로보어드바이저 시스템 등에 대한 실질적이고 실용적인 심화
        학습을 하고자 하는          학생들을 대상으로 함.
       본  과목은 학기 내내 최선의 노력을 다해 열심히 노력하고 끝까지 전념할 준비가 된
        학생들을 위한 과목임.
